item.content:encoded:
On Day 5 of the League Championship Series, one team broke a series tie ... will another advance to the Fall Classic?
After splitting the first two games in Tampa Bay, the Cleveland Guardians and Tampa Bay Rays faced off at Progressive Field in the day's first game. Thanks toPetey Halpin-- and his epic bat flip -- Cleveland prevailed, taking a 2-1 ALCS lead.
Tonight, in what could be the finale of the NLCS, the Milwaukee Brewers will look to continue their dominant championship series run and sweep the reigning champion Los Angeles Dodgers at Dodger Stadium. Can the Dodgers stave off elimination in Game 4 -- or will the Brewers advance to their first World Series since 1982?
Stay tuned for in-game action and postgame analysis from Los Angeles and Cleveland.
Key links: How final four teams were built | Playoff MVP tracker | Schedule
Cleveland leads series 2-1
It was over when ... Petey Halpin cranked a 96 mph sinker down the middle from Griffin Jax in the fifth inning. The ball landed deep into the right-field seats, 385 feet away, for a go-ahead two-run home run. Halpin flipped his bat nearly that high, too, and Cleveland didn't look back.
Game 3 star: Halpin, who began the season in Triple-A, had four big league home runs -- all during the regular season -- in 213 career plate appearances before Thursday. The center fielder's first postseason homer was the difference Thursday.
The stat that defined the game:The Rays' 13 strikeouts against Guardians pitching. The Rays posted the lowest strikeout rate in the majors this season at 18.8%. They struck out more than 12 times once, when they compiled 14 strikeouts against the Milwaukee Brewers back on March 30 in their fourth game of the season. Rays star Junior Caminero went 0-for-4 with four strikeouts -- matching a career high from 2025. So Thursday was an extreme outlier. Guardians starter Gavin Williams, the American League's strikeout leader this season, had nine strikeouts in five innings before four relievers combined for the remaining four punchouts. Tampa Bay will have to put the ball in play more to come back and win this series.
What it means for the rest of the series: With rain in the forecast Friday, there's a chance this series won't play Game 4 until Saturday. If so, the clubs would play Game 5 on Sunday, which would take away their travel day before a potential Game 6 in Tampa Bay on Monday. For now, Game 4 is scheduled for 6 p.m. ET Friday. -- Jorge Castillo
Highlights from the Guardians' win:
Halpin's homer, um, flips lead back to Guardians
Simpson silences Cleveland crowd with two-run triple
Gavin gettin' it done early
Guardians score first on Lowe's double
A series-defining day?

item.dc:creator: This article first appeared; Was Syndicated
item.description: Rawlings Gold Glove Award finalists for the National League and American League were announced, with the Los Angeles Dodgers having Max Muncy (third base) and Andy Pages (center field) placing among the top-three finishers at their respective positions. The 2026 season marks a fifth consecutive year in which the Dodgers have had multiple Gold Glove Award finalists. Mookie Betts (shortstop) and Miguel Rojas (utility) were last season’s representatives. From 2022-24, the Dodgers have had seven oth
item.content:encoded:
Rawlings Gold Glove Award finalists for the National League and American League were announced, with the Los Angeles Dodgers having Max Muncy (third base) and Andy Pages (center field) placing among the top-three finishers at their respective positions.
The 2026 season marks a fifth consecutive year in which the Dodgers have had multiple Gold Glove Award finalists. Mookie Betts (shortstop) and Miguel Rojas (utility) were last season’s representatives.
From 2022-24, the Dodgers have had seven other nominees. Betts has been the only Dodgers player to win a Gold Glove since 2022, as he took home the hardware for right field that year.
Gold Glove Award winners for the nine standard positions are determined via vote of MLB managers and up to six coaches from each team. Managers and coaches cannot vote for their own players and are only permitted to submit ballots for those in their same league.
Those votes amount to 75% of the selection total, with the SABR Defensive Index accounting for the remaining 25%.
The Toronto Blue Jays and Chicago Cubs had an MLB-best five players named finalists, with the Atlanta Braves, Arizona Diamondbacks, Texas Rangers and Kansas City Royals close behind at four apiece.
All 2026 Gold Glove Award winners will be announced live on ESPN on Sunday, Nov. 1.
For Muncy, it is his second career Gold Glove nomination and his first as a third baseman.
It is an impressive accomplishment for Muncy, improving his defense to such an extent in his age 36 season. He is looking to win his first career Gold Glove Award after falling short as a first baseman in 2021.
Alex Bregman (Chicago Cubs) and Javier Sanoja (Marlins) are the other two finalists.
Pages has been one of the best defensive center fielders in baseball since his breakout 2025 season.
In just his third season, he has already collected his first individual award this season as a representative in the Fall Classic.
It would be the first Gold Glove of his career if he can secure the votes. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts foresaw this outcome for the 25-year-old at the midpoint of the season.
Pages arm has arguably been his best weapon on defense this season, as he led the league with 13 outfield assists.
He is facing some stiff competition, with Pete Crow-Armstrong and Michael Harris II also up for consideration.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Miguel Rojas is getting rightfully roasted for fate-tempting cleats as Dodgers go down 3-0
item.dc:creator: Brandon Glick
item.description: These Los Angeles Dodgers broke a 25-year streak by becoming the first back-to-back champions with the World Series victory over the Toronto Blue Jays last year. Since then, all the talk about from the national media has been whether or not they could follow that 1998-2000 New York Yankees squad into the hallowed halls of three-peaters. item.content:encoded:
These Los Angeles Dodgers broke a 25-year streak by becoming the first back-to-back champions with the World Series victory over the Toronto Blue Jays last year.
Since then, all the talk about from the national media has been whether or not they could follow that 1998-2000 New York Yankees squad into the hallowed halls of three-peaters.
Down 2-0 to the Brewers in the NLCS, however, the goal of Game 3 was merely about survival. Which is why Miguel Rojas' cleats suggesting that a third title is on the horizon has naturally garnered quite a lot of attention on social media.
Now faced with the prospect of having to win four games in a row to even advance to the World Series, baseball fans may be waiting for that three-peat to load for quite a long time.
Dodgers have been humbled by Brewers, but they're equipped to make an improbable NLCS comeback
Because the Dodgers have been so dominant for so long, fans of other teams rarely miss their chance dunk on Los Angeles when the opportunity presents itself.
The good news for the Dodgers is that this series isn't over. A 3-0 deficit is daunting, but they're better equipped than most to come back from it. Tyler Glasnow will take the ball tonight against old friend Dustin May, giving Dave Roberts a clear advantage on the mound from the get-go.
If the Dodgers able to stave off the sweep at Chavez Ravine, they'll get one more game at home, this time with Tarik Skubal on the mound. Then, Game 6 in Milwaukee would allow them to deploy Yoshinobu Yamamoto again. After that would come a do-or-die Game 7 with Blake Snell eyeing a chance at redemption after Jake Bauers got the better of him last night.
That's a lot of looking ahead for a team that hasn't won a game in the NLCS to date, but it's a reminder of how stacked this roster is. Even with Jacob Misiorowski waiting in the wings, you'd have to like the Dodgers' chances of winning with Skubal and Yamamoto on the mound if they can get to their next starts.
It all starts with getting back in win column tonight and delaying the inevitable for another day. Failing that, Rojas may need to find the nearest dumpster in which to deposit his custom cleats.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Dave Roberts' Blake Snell decision was the tip of the iceberg in mortifying Dodgers Game 3 loss
item.dc:creator: Katrina Stebbins

In Game 2, Roberts had Brock Stewart intentionally walk Brice Turang in the sixth to get to the Brewers' hottest hitter in William Contreras, for seemingly no other reason than that the righty-righty matchup looked favorable on paper. Contreras hit a go-ahead single on the
item.content:encoded:
Dave Roberts has not been at his best in the NLCS, with the Los Angeles Dodgers facing the league-best Milwaukee Brewers in a best-of-seven that's making LA's NLDS against the Atlanta Braves look like the smallest of potatoes.
In Game 2, Roberts had Brock Stewart intentionally walk Brice Turang in the sixth to get to the Brewers' hottest hitter in William Contreras, for seemingly no other reason than that the righty-righty matchup looked favorable on paper. Contreras hit a go-ahead single on the first pitch Stewart served him.
That was small potatoes in contrast to Game 3, where Roberts seemed to make the worst possible decision at every conceivable turn. There is, of course, leaving Blake Snell in after he walked Andrew Vaughn to lead off the seventh, which then turned into a go-ahead, two-run homer for Jake Bauers ... and then a solo homer for Garrett Mitchell for some insurance.
The Dodgers went down 6-2, and their backs are now firmly against the wall. Roberts' Snell decision is the one that's going to be remembered least fondly, but there was a parade of other choices that all but doomed LA's three-peat hopes.
Dave Roberts' Blake Snell decision is obscuring smaller mistakes that doomed the Dodgers in NLCS Game 3
Roberts' next greatest sin, perhaps, was burning Josue De Paula in the bottom of the sixth. After Will Smith broke out of his slumber to hit a bases-loaded, go-ahead double, Roberts replaced Miguel Rojas with left Josue De Paula to face righty Abner Uribe. Milwaukee manager Pat Murphy countered by bringing in lefty DL Hall, so Roberts figured he would do play 3D chess and instead offered up righty Kiké Hernández, rendering De Paula unavailable for the rest of the game. Hernández struck out swinging.
There's the fact that Roberts started Tommy Edman, who had a single hit coming into Game 3. He went 0-for-4 on Wednesday night. There's the fact that he put Justin Wrobleski, who had a 6.13 ERA in the second half and was briefly demoted to Triple-A, in the game with the Dodgers down by two. Wrobleski quickly threw a wild pitch that allowed the Brewers' fifth run to score.
It might be going a little too far to say that this showing was legacy-threatening ... but it sure does feel like that right now. Roberts, no doubt, will be appropriately self-critical if the Dodgers' postseason road comes to an end after this series, but that doesn't erase how inexplicable his decisions in Game 3 were, and that they, alone, might've doomed LA.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers' Miguel Rojas slaps LA with reality check amid 3-0 NLCS deficit vs. Brewers appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Los Angeles Dodgers are staring at the brink of elimination, and Miguel Rojas is not sugarcoating how they got there. Los Angeles fell 6-2 to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series on Wednesday at Dodger Stadium, putting the two-time defending champions in a 3-0 series hole.
After the game, the veteran infielder offered a blunt explanation for the deficit. "To win championships, you've got to win moments. We haven't been able to do that in this series. They have," Rojas said, via MLB Network. "That's why we're 0-3 right now."
Game 3 was a perfect example. The Dodgers grabbed a 2-1 lead in the sixth inning when Will Smith lined a two-run double off Abner Uribe, and Blake Snell had retired 14 straight batters at one point after allowing a leadoff home run to Jackson Chourio on the first pitch of the game.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Milwaukee flipped it in the seventh. With a runner on, Jake Bauers won an 11-pitch battle against Snell and drilled a two-run homer to put the Brewers back in front. Garrett Mitchell followed with a solo blast, and Milwaukee tacked on runs in the eighth and ninth to pull away.
The big moments have gone the Brewers' way all series. Milwaukee won Game 1 by a 2-1 margin before taking Game 2 7-4, with its bullpen retiring all 15 Dodgers it faced to close out the second game.
The Dodgers' offense, meanwhile, has gone cold. Los Angeles has yet to hit a home run in the series, and it has struggled badly with runners in scoring position throughout the postseason.
Rojas knows the value of a big moment better than most. The 37-year-old is playing his final MLB season after returning to the Dodgers on a one-year deal, and he was one of the heroes of last year's World Series run.
Now, Los Angeles needs a lot of them in a hurry. The Dodgers have trailed 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series only once before, when the Baltimore Orioles swept them in the 1966 World Series.
They will try to stave off elimination in Game 4 on Thursday at Dodger Stadium, with the Brewers looking to complete a sweep and clinch their first National League pennant.
Related: Dodgers' Kyle Tucker makes 1 thing clear with LA facing NLCS elimination

item.title: [Orange County Register] Brewers push Dodgers to the brink, hit 3 homers off Blake Snell for 3-0 NLCS lead
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Reach out and feel the drywall. The Dodgers’ backs are up against it. The plucky little team that doesn’t hit home runs hit three of them off of Blake Snell on Wednesday night. The Milwaukee Brewers handed the Dodgers a 6-2 defeat in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series, pushing the back-to-back champions to the brink of elimination with the possibility of a sweep to avenge the one the Dodgers handed them last year. “It’s a pretty simple answer,” Max Muncy said when as
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Reach out and feel the drywall. The Dodgers’ backs are up against it.
The plucky little team that doesn’t hit home runs hit three of them off of Blake Snell on Wednesday night. The Milwaukee Brewers handed the Dodgers a 6-2 defeat in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series, pushing the back-to-back champions to the brink of elimination with the possibility of a sweep to avenge the one the Dodgers handed them last year.
“It’s a pretty simple answer,” Max Muncy said when asked how the Dodgers find themselves in this position. “We’re playing like (profanity). They’re playing great. It’s as simple as that. No need to overcomplicate it.”
Dreams of a three-peat on life support, the Dodgers’ thoughts now have to be on a ‘four-peat’ – it will take four consecutive victories for them to become just the second team in MLB history to come back from a 3-0 deficit to win a best-of-seven series. The 2004 Boston Red Sox (featuring a key stolen base by a reserve outfielder acquired at midseason from the Dodgers) did it in the American League Championship Series against the New York Yankees.
“If we lose, we’re done. We’ve got to go on one-game winning streaks four games in a row,” Kike’ Hernandez said.
“At the beginning of this year, we set out to do something historic,” Muncy said. “It looks like we’re going to have to make a little more history along the way if we want to accomplish that. That’s the task ahead of us. We still have the pitching staff to be able to do it. We just have to get some hits. If we can back our pitching staff then I know that, like I said, we have the pitching staff to do it.”
Tyler Glasnow is scheduled to start Game 4 on Thursday and try to save the Dodgers’ season. Muncy is correct — Glasnow won’t be able to do it without someone applying paddles to the Dodgers’ flatlining offense.
The Dodgers might not be going down without a fight. But so far, they are going down without any of the things it takes to make an offense successful in the postseason.
They are 2 for 16 with runners in scoring position in this series, 3 for 32 in the postseason. They have just two two-out hits in the three NLCS games (both singles) and only two extra-base hits (both doubles). The Dodgers hit 204 home runs in the regular season (tied for fourth in the National League) and eight more in their four-game National League Division Series victory over the Atlanta Braves (the most in the postseason to that point). They have hit none in the NLCS.
“They’re really good pitchers,” Miguel Rojas said. “A lot of their pitchers throw three different fastballs. They throw hard. They’ve been locating the ball really well. They haven’t really given us too many opportunities to build momentum.
“They’ve been attacking the zone. They trust their stuff in the zone. With all three fastballs, with a lot of guys that have a cutter, a sinker and a four-seam fastball, it’s really hard to kind of put barrels on the ball. So you’ve got to build some momentum that you can create with hits, but we haven’t been able to get a big hit.”
The Brewers have grabbed any momentum right back from the Dodgers. The Dodgers have scored in just five of the 27 innings so far. Four of those five times, the Brewers responded by scoring in the next half-inning themselves.
It happened again to turn Game 3.
Snell hadn’t give up a home run this year but Jackson Chourio sent the first pitch he threw Wednesday into the right-field pavilion. Snell thoroughly dominated the Brewers through six innings after that. He retired 18 of 20 batters after Chourio’s home run, striking out nine. Through the first five innings, the Brewers swung at 32 of Snell’s pitches and missed (17) more times than they made contact.
But the Dodgers’ lifeless offense did nothing against the Brewers’ second consecutive rookie starter, Robert Gasser, who held them scoreless on three hits and a walk through five innings.
Brewers manager Pat Murphy went to his bullpen after that, calling on Abner Uribe for the seventh time in their seven postseason games. When Uribe took the mound, the Brewers’ relievers had pitched 9⅔ scoreless innings in the NLCS and had allowed just one earned run in 28⅔ innings this postseason.
But Uribe walked the bases loaded, retiring just one batter. That brought up Will Smith – 1 for his first 25 this postseason. Smith jumped on a first-pitch fastball from Uribe and lined it off the wall in left-center field for a two-run double and a 2-1 lead.
It was the kind of clutch hit that Smith has provided time and time again over the years and had the stadium rocking.
Murphy made his next move, bringing in left-hander DL Hall with runners at second and third. Hall struck out pinch-hitter Kiké Hernandez and Tommy Edman as the Dodgers failed to capitalize on a chance to break the game open.
Snell went back out for the seventh inning having retired 14 in a row. But he walked Andrew Vaughn to start the inning and bring up Jake Bauers whose 12-pitch walk in the third inning of Game 2 was a critical turning point against Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
He did it again, extending his at-bat against Snell for 11 pitches and sending the last one, a fastball over the heart of the plate, into the right-field seats for a two-run home run. Two pitches later, Snell floated a changeup over the middle and Garrett Mitchell sent it on the same flight path as Bauers’ drive.
In 1,200⅔ career innings (regular season), Snell has only given up 15 home runs to left-handed hitters. Bauers and Mitchell did it back-to-back. The Brewers hit 154 home runs during the regular season, the fewest in the National League. They have outhomered the Dodgers 5-0 in the NLCS.
“I mean three home runs in a game — I didn’t give up one the whole year,” Snell said. “To have three in a game is pretty frustrating.”
The Brewers added single runs in the eighth and ninth innings to pull away.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dave Roberts Explain Dodgers' Lineup Shuffle for Game 3

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Shohei Ohtani will hit sixth Wednesday as Dave Roberts reshapes the Dodgers’ lineup for Game 3 against Milwaukee. Kyle Tucker moves to cleanup, Will Smith bats seventh, and Miguel Rojas starts against left-hander Robert Gasser, with Max Muncy available off the bench. Roberts said the changes give the order better balance and make it tougher for Milwaukee to work through its pitching matchups. With the Dodgers down 2–0, he also spoke about Ohtani’s late-night work and the intensity he expects from starter Blake Snell.
“Shohei’s all on board”
Roberts sees Tucker as a good fit in the middle of the order against both Gasser and the relievers who may follow him.
“I love the length of the lineup,” Roberts said. “Kyle has been, throughout his career and currently, agnostic with pitchers left versus right. Gasser is a guy they’re probably going to run two times through the lineup. If it gets a little beyond that, I like Kyle there.”
Smith moves down again after batting fifth in Game 2. Roberts hopes a different spot will help the catcher’s at-bats fall into place.
“Give the player a different look, let the game come to him,” he said. “Last game, there were some good swings in there, which I’m really encouraged about. Having him there around the wraparound of the lineup, I think, is going to be a good thing.”
“I’ve got Miggy in there, which I’m excited about, having Miggy versus a left-hander and then deploying Max whenever the time makes sense.”
Ohtani’s move is part of that effort to spread out the left-handed and right-handed bats.
“It’s more what gives our lineup the best balance,” Roberts said. “Separating the lefties, the righties, making it a little more difficult for them to navigate our lineup. Shohei’s all on board. Whatever it takes to win.”
Ohtani puts in the work
Roberts said Ohtani stayed late Tuesday to work on his swing and talk with teammates about beating Milwaukee.
“As far as him as a person, he couldn’t be more of a team player, more agreeable,” Roberts said. “He was here late last night working on his swing, out with the guys and talking about things, how we’re going to beat these guys.”
“God, it couldn’t be more of a joy. This guy is great for our game. He’s great for all of us.”
Roberts saw a sharper focus in that work.
“He expects a lot from himself, obviously, and he hasn’t performed to his expectations,” he said. “It’s up to all of us to do our jobs. But this was a different look from Shohei yesterday.”
“He was determined, and that’s an understatement.”
Snell’s “slow burn”
Snell gets the ball after a disappointing NLDS start against Atlanta. Roberts has noticed a quieter pitcher waiting for his next chance.
“Much more quiet, staying to himself more,” he said. “He’s been really anxious to get another opportunity. Still being a part of the team and cheering for guys, but this has been a slow burn since that last outing.”
“When you see him take the mound today, you’re going to see another level of intensity. For me, it’s making sure you manage that intensity because it’s already a big game.”
Roberts also likes the thought Snell has put into understanding Milwaukee’s approach.
“He’s a very cerebral, thoughtful person,” Roberts said. “To understand the psyche of your opponent is important because it adds to his edge, his focus, knowing how hungry and feisty and tough that team is.”
“Being aggressive to match their intensity, I like that exercise and what he’s been doing.”
Make the relievers work
Roberts wants more sustained at-bats against a Brewers bullpen that has held the Dodgers scoreless through two games.
“Mookie’s done a good job of still winning pitches, competing in at-bats,” he said. “Other guys, we’ve got to have that same level of fight against those guys versus one-, two-pitch outs.”
“Ashby has been very efficient against us. You’ve got to go through the pain of an at-bat, the grind of it, to ultimately have those guys make a mistake. We could do a better job of that.”
Betts’ work has stood out beyond his batting line.
“He’s playing really high-level baseball,” Roberts said. “If you watch the games, he’s seeing a ton of pitches. He’s getting on base. He’s moving guys over, and that’s what you have to do to win playoff games.”
“There are a couple more big hits in there, maybe a homer. I love the way he’s playing. He’s in a good frame of mind right now, and he’s playing next-level shortstop as well.”
Everything goes into tonight
Roberts plans to manage Game 3 with the urgency its place in the series demands.
“We still have to win four games, but the most important game is tonight,” he said. “We’re going to do everything we can to win this one, and our guys understand how important this one is.”
“It’s good to be home. Those guys fed off their crowd, and I’m excited to see some blue towels and some noise tonight and have our guys feed off it.”
For Roberts, keeping the focus on one game also helps keep the task manageable.
“Guys love to compete. I love to compete,” he said. “We all know what’s at stake. It’s going to be fun. There’s some pressure there, but you’ve got to embrace this.”
“When you start thinking about winning four games, I get nervous. But I think we can manage winning a game tonight.”

item.content:encoded:
The NLCS resumes at Dodger Stadium on Wednesday, with the Dodgers looking to embark on a comeback down 2-0 in the series against the Milwaukee Brewers.
The top three in the lineup remain the same, as Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman and Teoscar Hernández hit in the top three spots. The middle of the lineup received an adjustment that comes as little to no surprise with how Shohei Ohtani and Will Smith have hit in the postseason.
Kyle Tucker moves up to cleanup in the starting lineup, the highest spot in the order he's been placed in this October. After a rough regular season, Tucker has found his stride at the plate at the bottom of the lineup, slashing .300/.391/.500 with a home run and two RBI over six games. Tucker has faced Milwaukee's Game 3 starter Robert Gasser twice in his career, collecting three hits across six at-bats including a home run.
Andy Pages has also impressed at the plate this postseason, turning the page on what was a historically awful title run at the plate last year. The 2026 All-Star has five hits across 20 at-bats, with his highlights being his go-ahead, two-run single in Game 4 of the NLDS and for getting the Dodgers on the board against Jacob Misiorowski in Game 1 of the NLCS. Pages has gone hitless since his Game 1 RBI single, but he moves up to fifth in the lineup against Gasser, also the highest spot he's hit in the postseason this year.
The elephant in the room is Shohei Ohtani getting moved all the way down to sixth in the lineup. Ohtani was adamant about playing in Game 3, and Dave Roberts ultimately granted his wish.
"He's adamant he feels good enough to be in there. He's close to finding something with his swing. I feel great about it," manager Dave Roberts said Tuesday just before the Dodgers workout at Dodger Stadium. "He was very convicted that he is onto something mechanically. He was adamant that he can help us. He's well enough to help us win a baseball game. So that's all I needed to hear."
Try as he might to will his way into the lineup, Ohtani has been a detriment offensively since hitting his final regular season home run on Aug. 18 in Denver, and he's carried that funk over the team's six playoff games slashing just .150/.261/.150 with zero RBI. Ohtani had never hit as low as second in the lineup until Game 3 of the NLDS, and it's the first time Ohtani is hitting sixth in the lineup since Sept. 19, 2020 back when he was with the Angels.
Will Smith has also struggled mightily this October, and he slides all the way down to seventh in the starting lineup. Miguel Rojas gets the start at third base over Max Muncy against the left-hander Gasser, and Tommy Edman gets the start at second base, rounding things out in the lineup. Blake Snell makes his first start since getting the ball for Game 2 of the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves.

item.content:encoded:
Game 3 of the National League Championship Series between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers at Dodger Stadium is scheduled to start at 5:00 p.m. PDT on Wednesday.
The Brewers won the first two games of the series on Sunday and Monday.
Milwaukee won the first game 2-1 and the second game 7-4.
Before Wednesday’s game, Mookie Betts dropped an honest quote on Shohei Ohtani, who has struggled significantly this postseason.
Dodgers Star Mookie Betts Makes Honest Shohei Ohtani Statement Amid Brewers Series
MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN – OCTOBER 12: Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers reacts in the third inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game two of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 12, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images)
“I couldn’t imagine really having the expectations that he has and falling short in a way that it’s not normal for him,” Betts said to reporters, including USA Today’s Bob Nightengale. “Then having to come back and be present in the postseason knowing how important he is to the boys.”
“He’s trying. It’s just really, really hard. It’s really hard to make these slight adjustments in this short amount of time. Like I said, it took me almost two years. I feel for him. I know he’s grinding, he’s working. So we’ll just see. We’ll see how he comes and prepares.”
MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN – OCTOBER 12: Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers walks back to the dugout after striking out in the first inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game two of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 12, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images)
“But I know he’s giving it his all. We can at least lay our heads on a pillow at night knowing that we’ve given it everything.”
This postseason, Ohtani has gone 3-for-20 with seven strikeouts and three walks. He is dealing with biceps and knee injuries.
Looking at NLCS Game 3 Between Dodgers and Brewers
MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN – OCTOBER 11: Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers hits a fly ball against the Milwaukee Brewers during the eighth inning in game one of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 11, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images)
The Dodgers considered benching Ohtani for Game 3, but ultimately placed him in the lineup.
Ohtani is batting sixth, a career low, as the DH today.
MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN – OCTOBER 12: Shohei Ohtani #17 of the Los Angeles Dodgers returns to the dugout after grounding out in the third inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game two of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field on October 12, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images)
Here is the Dodgers’ lineup:
- Mookie Betts SS
- Freddie Freeman 1B
- Teoscar Hernandez LF
- Kyle Tucker RF
- Andy Pages CF
- Shohei Ohtani DH
- Will Smith C
- Miguel Rojas 3B
- Tommy Edman 2B
Left-hander Blake Snell will start for the Dodgers today. Southpaw Robert Gasser is slated to start for the Brewers.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are set for a pivotal Game Three in their NLCS with the Milwaukee Brewers.
Milwaukee holds a 2-0 lead, and if the Dodgers want to advance to the World Series, they must win four of the next five games, which will certainly be a tall task.
However, the series has now shifted to LA, and the Dodgers have another ace in Blake Snell taking the ball on Wednesday evening.
Before the NLCS Game Three, the Dodgers revealed their lineup to try and muster runs off southpaw Robert Gasser, and Max Muncy is not featured in the group.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Issued Strong Anthony Volpe Take Amid Major Decision
Dodgers’ Max Muncy OUT of Game Three Batting Order
Likely due to the Brewers throwing a southpaw the Dodgers way in Game 3, Max Muncy is not featured in the batting order, but he will likely be used in a pinch-hit scenario if Milwaukee deploys a RHP at some in the game to face Miguel Rojas, who is IN at 3B in Muncy’s place.
@UnderdogMLB help break the news of the full Dodgers lineup for 10/14:
Dodgers 10/14: “M. Betts SS F. Freeman 1B T. Hernández LF K. Tucker RF A. Pages CF S. Ohtani DH W. Smith C M. Rojas 3B T. Edman 2B B. Snell SP”
Other lineup notes include: Both Shohei Ohtani and Will Smith dropping in the order, Kyle Tucker getting the start at cleanup, and Teoscar Hernandez batting third.
Tommy Edman is also getting a start, while the Dodgers are relying on a strong start from Blake Snell.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are facing a must-win in Game Three of the NLCS against the Milwaukee Brewers on Wednesday evening.
The good news for the Dodgers is that the series is shifting back to Los Angeles. Blake Snell will get the start for LA on Wednesday evening, and he will oppose Robert Gasser.
Before the game started, the Dodgers announced their Game Three lineup, which featured a major Will Smith decision.
More MLB on Heavy: Los Angeles Dodgers Announce Blake Snell News Before Pivotal Brewers Game
Will Smith Dropped in Los Angeles Dodgers Batting Order
When the Dodgers Game Three lineup dropped on Wednesday afternoon, it came with a few surprises.
In two big developments, Will Smith and Shohei Ohtani have dropped in the batting order.
Here is the full group, per @UnderdogMLB:
Dodgers 10/14: “M. Betts SS F. Freeman 1B T. Hernández LF K. Tucker RF A. Pages CF S. Ohtani DH W. Smith C M. Rojas 3B T. Edman 2B B. Snell SP”
The flip to Will Smith being demoted in the lineup is that Kyle Tucker has moved up several spots and will bat cleanup against the Brewers’ LHP Gasser.
Shohei Ohtani bats sixth, and Tommy Edman/Miguel Rojas are getting starts in the infield, while Max Muncy gets the pine.
More MLB on Heavy: Toronto Blue Jays Predicted to Poach Yankees All-Star for $80 Million
Taking a Quick Look at Will Smith’s 2026 Season
LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA – MAY 08: Will Smith #16 of the Los Angeles Dodgers during a 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves at Dodger Stadium on May 08, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images)
As did many of the Los Angeles Dodgers (at some point in 2026), Will Smith spent a good chunk of time on the Injured List with a neck issue.
He got a handful of starts down the stretch of the regular season, but he’s been really struggling at the plate in the MLB playoffs, and after moving him down for Game Two, manager Dave Roberts is now demoting him to the 7-spot in the lineup.
Perhaps it’s a wake-up call for Smith, but as the Dodgers search for the right lineup combination, having Smith (who is 1-for-20+) in the 3-hole just isn’t going to get things going.
It will be interesting to see if this decision pays off for Roberts and the rest of the Dodgers.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Issued Strong Anthony Volpe Take Amid Major Decision

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers hope to punch back in the NLCS with a home win in Game 3 over the Milwaukee Brewers.
The Dodgers are down 0-2 in the series, but hope isn’t lost; this Dodgers team thrives when it’s backed into a corner. To turn things around, the offense needs to convert on scoring chances.
Dodgers’ Lineup vs. Brewers
1. Mookie Betts, SS
2. Freddie Freeman, 1B
3. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
4. Kyle Tucker, RF
5. Andy Pages, CF
6. Shohei Ohtani, DH
7. Will Smith, C
8. Miguel Rojas, 3B
9. Tommy Edman, 2B
The Dodgers announced Tuesday that Shohei Ohtani will play despite his struggles and injuries. He will stay in the 6-hole, his lowest spot yet for the Dodgers.
The Brewers are rolling out lefty Robert Gasser, who possesses some matchup problems. Naturally, right-handers Teoscar Hernandez and Andy Pages are moving up from their usual positions.
Will Smith, who has also struggled in the postseason, is moving down to his lowest spot in a while.
Other than shuffling players around, Roberts is sticking with the same group from Game 2, with the only exception being Miguel Rojas at third base while Max Muncy sits.
Who is pitching for the Dodgers?
Blake Snell takes the mound for the Dodgers in the biggest spot of his career. The team needs him to deliver a great outing to keep their three-peat hopes alive against a game Brewers team.
Snell has posted a 1.90 ERA over 42.2 innings this year. In the postseason, he hasn’t been as sharp in one start. He pitched just 3.2 innings in Game 2 of the NLDS, allowing one run but giving up five walks and three hits.
Against this crop of Brewers hitters, they’re hitting only 11-for-64 with a .172 average, a .274 OBP, and 29 strikeouts.
If Snell does well in this game, his legacy as a Dodger and pitcher will grow exponentially.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers drew six walks during Game 1 of the NLCS, including one from rookie sensation Josue De Paula in the top of the ninth inning.
De Paula pinch-hit for Kiké Hernández with the Dodgeres down 2-1, two outs, and a runner on first base. He drew a five-pitch walk against Milwaukee Brewers closer Trevor Megill, which prompted former Cincinnati Reds great and current NBC analyst Joey Votto to heap praise upon the Dodgers' 21-year-old-prospect.
"De Paula about to be in that upper tier quick, quick.," Votto wrote on X (formerly Twitter) during Sunday's game. In the comments of his tweet, the former MVP went on to mention De Paula's beautiful swing and elite swing-decisions.
The high-end comparison for De Paula has always been Yordan Alvarez, who the Dodgers famously once had in their pipeline. One can assume the likely 2026 AL MVP is certainly a player in Votto's so-called "upper tier" of hitters in MLB. De Paula didn't even swing the bat during his plate appearance in Game 1, but the seeds are being planted for what should be an incredibly successful career.
Dodgers' Josue De Paula is turning heads and could force tough managerial decisions in the playoffs
De Paula now has two walks in his three plate appearances during the postseason. His previous one came during the seventh inning of Game 4 of the NLDS, which allowed the Dodgers to score the go-ahead and game-winning runs to seal the series and advance to the NLCS.
Manager Dave Roberts could swap De Paula for the likes of Hernández, Tommy Edman, or Miguel Rojas. So far, during the postseason, the Dodgers are hitting .207/.282/.360/.642 in the postseason and De Paula's presence on the bench could help alleviate what has been an underwhelming postseason offensively for the reigning back-to-back World Series champions.
It takes every single player on the roster having a clutch moment for a team to win a World Series, and De Paula is showing that he is more than capable of providing an invaluable at bat if he is deployed properly.
De Paula's impressive, yet inconsequential, walk in Game 1 might already have Dodgers fans questioning Teoscar Hernandez's future this offseason. Unless De Paula can learn a new position on the fly like Mookie Betts, he'll completely blocked from the starting lineup by Hernandez, Andy Pages, Kyle Tucker, in 2027.

item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE –– Entering Monday night, the Dodgers were not giving serious consideration to removing Shohei Ohtani from their lineup.
One big loss, and four ugly at-bats later, however, that previously steadfast plan suddenly seemed capable of changing.
Following a 7-4 defeat to the Milwaukee Brewers that put the Dodgers in a two-game hole in their National League Championship Series, the team was set to re-evaluate Ohtani’s status ahead of Game 3 on Wednesday.
Manager Dave Roberts told The Athletic that the team would have “a conversation” with Ohtani about whether or not he would be in the lineup for the contest. A source with knowledge of the situation confirmed to the California Post that the decision would come down to whether Ohtani still felt healthy enough to remain the starting designated hitter, as ESPN also reported.
The development came after Ohtani’s worst performance this postseason, in which he went 0-for-4 with two strikeouts.
Over six games in these playoffs, the four-time MVP is now just 3-for-20 with only three singles, two walks and seven strikeouts while battling ongoing right arm and left knee issues –– playing at what the team has repeatedly acknowledged is well less than 100%.
Despite all that, the Dodgers have also been holding out hope for a revival from their two-way superstar. Roberts promised Ohtani would “come to life” eventually. President of baseball operations Andrew Friedman predicted that “at some point, it’s going to click for him.”
Now, however, the Dodgers might not be able to keep waiting around for Ohtani magic.
After back-to-back losses to open the NLCS in Milwaukee this week, they return home to Los Angeles just two more defeats away from elimination –– and only one from a 3-0 deficit that just one team in MLB history (Roberts’ iconic Boston Red Sox squad in the 2004 American League Championship Series) has ever come back from.
“Can we [come back in this series]? Absolutely,” Roberts said. “But it’s just, you want to get that first [win].”
Prior to Monday, Ohtani had at least reached base safely in each of his first five playoff games.
Instead of continuing to progress with his swing, however, his 0-fer in Game 2 represented a notable step back.
Before the game, the injury-hampered 32-year-old took batting practice on the field for a third-straight day –– a drastic, and telling, change of routine for someone who normally never hits outside of the indoor batting cages.
During his BP sessions, coaches had been encouraged by the look of his swing, optimistically noting the fact he was driving the ball to the big part of the field.
“I feel good [with] where he’s at,” Roberts said Sunday. “[He is] certainly not 100 percent, but it’s good enough.”
Advertisement
That, however, was no longer the case in Tuesday’s demoralizing loss, when the Dodgers’ offense as a whole managed just three hits, made outs in all 15 of their at-bats against Brewers relievers, and suddenly looked like a unit in desperate need of a jolt.
Ohtani didn’t provide one. Instead, he looked even more lost than ever before.
He ended the first inning with a three-pitch strikeout, chasing an elevated fastball from Brewers rookie Logan Henderson. He stranded a runner at second to end the second, flailing at another high fastball for a softly hit grounder to third. Then came the sixth, when Ohtani was so fooled by a slider from left-handed reliever JoJo Romero that his bat flung out of his hands on his unsuccessful attempt to check his swing.
He would make one more out in the ninth, lifting a harmless fly ball to left field off top Brewers southpaw Aaron Ashby.
Once again, he did not address reporters postgame, still yet to speak publicly since before the start of the NLDS.
If the Dodgers were to drop Ohtani from the lineup for Game 3 –– when the Brewers will start left-hander Robert Gasser –– the team would have several potential ways to fill his void at DH.
The most obvious one: rookie sensation Josue De Paula.
The 21-year-old has only logged 45 total big-league plate appearances since being called up straight from double-A back in September, but has reached safely in more than half of them.
That includes a pair of impressive walks as a pinch-hitter in recent days; one that helped set up a game-winning rally in Game 4 of the NL Division Series, and another in an ultimately failed ninth-inning comeback bid in Game 1 of the NLCS on Sunday.
Granted, swapping even a diminished version of Ohtani for someone so inexperienced would undoubtedly be a stunning decision on the surface. And if this series weren’t 2-0 for the Brewers, the calculus would be different.
But right now, De Paula might be just as much of an on-base threat, and (given he is fully healthy) is perhaps an even more likely candidate to potentially slug the ball.
And, at this increasingly dire stage, the Dodgers can ill-afford to risk another empty performance from their biggest star.
If not De Paula, the Dodgers could also use the DH spot to potentially fit October hero, and right-handed hitter, Kiké Hernández back in the lineup, after he was dropped back to the bench for Game 2 in favor of Tommy Edman. Perhaps it could also be a way to get Miguel Rojas in as another extra righty bat, especially while he nurses a back injury he suffered in the NLDS.
None of these scenarios, of course, are what the Dodgers wanted to be contemplating so soon into their World Series three-peat bid.
But suddenly, with the stakes rising higher and Ohtani’s performance trending in the opposite direction, all options might need to be on the table.
The best player in baseball, at least in his current physical condition, might need to be benched.

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Commentary: Dodgers' three-peat dreams are on life support as the deflated heroes return home
item.dc:creator: Bill Plaschke
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article - Bill Plaschke writes the Dodgers’ three-peat dreams are dying in the face of the potent Milwaukee Brewers. - The Dodgers’ aces have struggled to stay on the mound deep in games and key bats have gone silent. - After a humbling 7-4 loss in Game 2, the Dodgers need a miraculous rejuvenation at Dodger Stadium to extend their season. Once brimming with life, the Dodgers’ historic quest has curled up into a withered heap. The three-peat is dying. The three-pea
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
- Bill Plaschke writes the Dodgers’ three-peat dreams are dying in the face of the potent Milwaukee Brewers.
- The Dodgers’ aces have struggled to stay on the mound deep in games and key bats have gone silent.
- After a humbling 7-4 loss in Game 2, the Dodgers need a miraculous rejuvenation at Dodger Stadium to extend their season.
Once brimming with life, the Dodgers’ historic quest has curled up into a withered heap.
The three-peat is dying.
The three-peat is slowly, agonizingly having the life squeezed out of it by a collection of hardscrabble Midwesterners with no regard for stardom or status.
After two games of the National League Championship Series, the three-peat was formally been placed on life support Monday after the mighty Dodgers lost a second consecutive game to those little giants known as Milwaukee Brewers.
This time the final score was 7-4 after another devastating night at American Family Field, and now the Dodgers trail two-games-to-none in a best-of-seven series that appears beyond their control.
For a second consecutive game, their ace was knocked out. For a second consecutive game, their powerful offense petered out.
For a second consecutive game, they looked like a weary, aging band of fallen stars that had stumbled into a surprisingly deep pothole and had no idea how to climb out.
For the Dodgers to win this series and continue their journey toward a third consecutive championship, they must beat the Brewers in four of the next five games, the last two of which will be played in Milwaukee.
It doesn’t seem likely. It doesn’t even seem possible.
Not once in during their previous two title seasons did they trail anybody two-games- to-none, and they certainly don’t seem equipped to survive it now.
The Milwaukee Brewers dealt a blow to the Dodgers’ October psyche with their NLCS Game 1 win, but the Dodgers have shown they’re capable of bouncing back.
Look at how they lost on Monday. On second thought, don’t look, because what you’ll see bears scant resemblance to the swaggering, self-assured Dodgers of postseasons past.
They pitched their October ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and he’s always saved them, right? Not this time. He couldn’t make it out of the third inning, battered by scattered wildness and scathing swings.
They were handed runs on two errors by the Brewers shaky rookie starter Logan Henderson, and they’ve always capitalized, right? Not this time. They couldn’t make the Brewers pay for their clumsiness, managing just three total hits, the slumps of their superstars ever deepening, Will Smith and Shohei Ohtani now becoming absolute offensive liabilities.
Even with all this, they sent Henderson packing after four innings and took aim at a heavily used Brewer bullpen and surely they could summon the firepower to send at least one of those relievers running, right? Not this time, as four Brewer relievers set a major-league postseason record by pitching five perfect innings.
The last two innings being a sad microcosm of the previous seven.
Entering the eighth inning, the Dodgers only trailed 4-3 and had the top of their order coming up in what could have still been a trademark Dodger October comeback.
Not so fast.
Facing Abner Uribe, Mookie Betts struck out. Facing Aaron Ashby, Freddie Freeman struck out and Teoscar Hernández grounded out. Yeah, with perhaps their entire season on the line, they couldn’t even get the ball out of the infield.
The Brewers, of course, sealed the deal with two runs on three singles in the bottom of the eighth, and the Dodgers went meekly 1-2-3 in the ninth.
It was surely, truly painful for Dodger fans to witness the final out, a strikeout by … yep, last season’s World Series hero Miguel Rojas.
The three-peat is dying, and it’s almost unbearable to watch.
Having watched both of their top two aces beaten in Milwaukee, the Dodgers will now come home with Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow starting in Game 3 and 4.
In any other scenario, both pitchers are aces as well and the Dodgers would have a huge advantage. But neither pitcher has looked great in the postseason and both will be pitching while bearing the weight of a stressed-out Dodger nation..
What could possibly stand in the way of the Dodgers becoming just the third franchise to win three World Series in a row? Plenty, it turns out.
“Yeah, it’s certainly a challenge,” said manager Dave Roberts. “I think that, if you look Game 3, I like where we’re at as far as in a vacuum, who’s pitching, where our bullpen is at, being at home. Then you’ve got to go from there.”
Roberts still has hope. But he’s not looking past Game 3.
“As far as can we do it, absolutely, but it’s just you want to get that first one,” he said.
Dodger Stadium will be filled with fans in what could be a celebration. Or a wake.

item.content:encoded:
Brewers' Pat Murphy sends warning to Tarik Skubal before NLCS Game 1 appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
The Milwaukee Brewers are getting ready to take on the Los Angeles Dodgers, in the National League Championship Series. Brewers manager Pat Murphy is sending a message to Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal, before Game 1.
That message is a powerful one.
"I want to step on his throat," Murphy said, per WFRV-TV in Wisconsin.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
The Dodgers and Brewers play Game 1 on Sunday night. Milwaukee's players are ready to go.
"Coming into the postseason, you had a feeling you were going to have to go through L.A.," Brewers designated hitter Christian Yelich said, per MLB.com. "They're back-to-back champs, and they're a great team. We have a lot of respect for those guys.
"At the same time, we feel like we can play with anybody when we play our game. When we play our brand of baseball, when we play clean and execute, we're a really hard team to beat. We're going to go in there and grind."
It will be a tough challenge for the Brewers against Skubal. Skubal famously was traded to Los Angeles this season from the Detroit Tigers, ahead of the MLB trade deadline.
"Skubal showed exactly why the Dodgers swung big to acquire him from the Tigers ahead of the Trade Deadline in his NLDS Game 1 start, when he struck out seven across six innings of one-run ball against the Braves. Now, he will take the hill as L.A. begins the next stage of its title defense," MLB.com added.
The Brewers had an outstanding season in the National League. The team won the NL Central, and won 103 games. Milwaukee has done just about everything the last few years but make a World Series.
That is because the Dodgers have always stood in the way. Los Angeles is looking for their third consecutive World Series title this season.
Time will tell if this is finally the year that the Brewers break through that glass ceiling.

item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers released their lineup for Game 1 of the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday, and the placement of Kyle Tucker once again drew attention. Manager Dave Roberts slotted the outfielder eighth in the order despite the presence of right-hander Jacob Misiorowski on the mound for Milwaukee, a matchup that might otherwise favor a left-handed bat higher in the lineup, via Underdog MLB. Tucker has occupied that lower spot throughout the postse
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers released their lineup for Game 1 of the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday, and the placement of Kyle Tucker once again drew attention.
Manager Dave Roberts slotted the outfielder eighth in the order despite the presence of right-hander Jacob Misiorowski on the mound for Milwaukee, a matchup that might otherwise favor a left-handed bat higher in the lineup, via Underdog MLB.
Tucker has occupied that lower spot throughout the postseason, including during the Dodgers’ series against the Atlanta Braves.
The decision keeps him in right field while the top of the order features Mookie Betts at shortstop, Freddie Freeman at first base, Will Smith catching, and Shohei Ohtani as the designated hitter batting cleanup. Teoscar Hernández, Max Muncy, and Andy Pages follow before Tucker, with Enrique Hernández handling second base in place of the unavailable Tommy Edman and Miguel Rojas.
Tarik Skubal, acquired from Detroit at the trade deadline, starts for Los Angeles opposite Misiorowski in the series opener at American Family Field.
The arrangement reflects a broader pattern for Tucker in his first season with the Dodgers. After signing a four-year, $240 million contract in free agency, choosing the defending champions over longer offers elsewhere, he posted a .233 batting average with 17 home runs and 70 RBIs across 154 regular-season games.
Those numbers fell short of the production many expected from a player who had delivered multiple 30-home-run seasons earlier in his career. Roberts and the front office have nonetheless kept him in the everyday mix, banking on the October performance that motivated the signing in the first place.
Tucker has shown signs of that form since early September and carried it into the Division Series. He went 5-for-15 with a home run, two RBIs, and two stolen bases against Atlanta, batting .333 in limited action.
Those at-bats included a two-run homer in the series opener at Dodger Stadium.
With the Dodgers seeking a third consecutive World Series appearance, the NLCS against a Brewers club that won 103 games offers the clearest stage yet for the 29-year-old to justify the investment.
A productive stretch against Milwaukee’s pitching staff would quiet questions about his regular-season output and reinforce the club’s bet that his best baseball remains ahead.
For now, the eighth spot keeps Tucker in the lineup without disrupting the balance Roberts has settled on for the series.
Both clubs enter the matchup after efficient Division Series victories, and the early pitching duel between Skubal and Misiorowski sets a high bar for the hitters behind them.
Tucker’s ability to contribute from the lower third of the order will factor into whether Los Angeles can seize an early advantage on the road.

item.content:encoded:
grandes ligas
Dodgers mantienen a Miguel Rojas en su roster de la Serie de Campeonato
Los Cerveceros mantuvieron el mismo grupo de 26 jugadores que tuvieron para su serie divisional de la Liga Nacional contra San Diego.
El venezolano Miguel Rojas fue incluido en el roster de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles para la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional, después de haber estado fuera por dolor en la parte baja de la espalda.
El zurdo Justin Wrobleski también forma parte del roster de los Dodgers para el duelo ante Milwaukee. Los Cerveceros mantuvieron el mismo grupo de 26 jugadores que tuvieron para su serie divisional de la Liga Nacional contra San Diego.
El Juego 1 de la NLCS se disputa la noche del domingo.
A Rojas le realizaron pruebas después de que salió durante la victoria 3-1 de los Dodgers en Atlanta en el Juego 3 de la serie divisional de la Liga Nacional. Las imágenes mostraron en su mayoría problemas previos de espalda.
El infielder veterano entrenó con Los Ángeles el sábado en el American Family Field, y el mánager Dave Roberts indicó que Rojas probablemente formaría parte del roster de la NLCS.
El jugador de 37 años conectó el jonrón del empate en la novena entrada del Juego 7 de la Serie Mundial el año pasado en Toronto, para ayudar a los Dodgers a ganar su segundo campeonato consecutivo. Ha manifestado que se inclina por retirarse al final de la temporada.
La incorporación de Wrobleski le da a los Dodgers 13 lanzadores en su roster de la NLCS, después de que llevaron 12 para su serie contra los Bravos. Wrobleski, de 26 años, tuvo marca de 12-5 con efectividad de 3,66 en 22 aperturas y seis apariciones como relevista este año, y fue seleccionado por primera vez al equipo de estrellas de la Liga Nacional.
El infielder Hyeseong Kim quedó fuera del roster de los Dodgers para la NLCS. Participó en un juego contra Atlanta como reemplazo defensivo.

item.content:encoded:
Según el mánager Dave Roberts, el de Los Teques mejoró notablemente luego de una infiltración de cortisona en la zona lumbar
Miguel Rojas está listo para la serie de campeonato con Dodgers.-Miguel Rojas apunta a ser titular en la Serie de Campeonato tras superar molestias físicas sufridas en los últimos días y que lo apartaron del duelo ante Bravos de Atlanta la semana pasada.
El infielder venezolano Miguel Rojas tuvo que abandonar el tercer compromiso de la Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional a causa de una dolencia lumbar, lo que también le impidió estar en el cuarto choque. Sin embargo, el estratega Dave Roberts confirmó ante los medios de comunicación que confía en incluir al experimentado jugador en el roster para la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional, luego de que una infiltración de cortisona aliviara favorablemente el malestar en la zona.
Lea también: Reactivan Pdval para atender a 3.500 familias en Puerto La Cruz
Según lo indicado por el mánager todavía no tiene claro si el oriundo de Los Teques pueda estar de titular en el duelo frente a Milwaukee de este domingo. Pero si que pueda ser utilizado como un bateador emergente determinante desde la banca ante los lanzadores zurdos.
Conviene recordar que Rojas se consolidó como una figura clave en el séptimo partido de la Serie Mundial del año pasado, cuando empató las acciones de forma agónica mediante un jonrón en la novena entrada ante el cerrador de los Blue Jays, Jeff Hoffman. El veterano aporta un recorrido invaluable a la plantilla angelina al contar con dos anillos de campeón y 23 compromisos de experiencia en fases decisivas de octubre.
EO//Con información de: Líder

item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee
item.description: - Shohei Ohtani, que acabó con de 13 al bate en la NLDS, realizó una sesión de prácticas de bateo en un intento por recuperar su swing antes del primer partido de la NLCS de los Dodgers contra los Cerveceros. - El entrenador Dave Roberts sigue confiando en que Ohtani pueda salir de su bache, pero este se enfrentará a una dura prueba contra el as de los Cerveceros, Jacob Misiorowski. MILWAUKEE — Shohei Ohtani lanzó con fuerza una bola que llegó hasta la segunda grada del campo central-derecho. A
item.content:encoded:
- Shohei Ohtani, que acabó con de 13 al bate en la NLDS, realizó una sesión de prácticas de bateo en un intento por recuperar su swing antes del primer partido de la NLCS de los Dodgers contra los Cerveceros.
- El entrenador Dave Roberts sigue confiando en que Ohtani pueda salir de su bache, pero este se enfrentará a una dura prueba contra el as de los Cerveceros, Jacob Misiorowski.
MILWAUKEE — Shohei Ohtani lanzó con fuerza una bola que llegó hasta la segunda grada del campo central-derecho. A continuación, lanzó otra, esta vez un poco más cerca de la imponente pantalla de vídeo que se alza sobre el American Family Field y en la que se veía el enorme logotipo “2026 NLCS”.
«Ha sido un buen día de trabajo para él», afirmó el entrenador de bateo Aaron Bates tras el entrenamiento de los Dodgers del sábado. «Él y Bookie [Mookie Betts] habían estado hablando sobre el bateo estos últimos días. Fue idea suya batear en el campo. Nuevo campo, nuevo escenario, ese tipo de cosas».
Ohtani solo ha bateado en prácticas de bateo en un campo unas pocas veces esta temporada. Pero antes del primer partido de la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional contra los Milwaukee Brewers el domingo, realizó una sesión prolongada con la máquina de lanzamiento.
“Simplemente intenta no girar el barril demasiado pronto”, explicó Bates sobre en qué se ha centrado Ohtani desde el punto de vista mecánico. “Sentirse cómodo en la para que sienta que está en una buena posición para batear, pero sobre todo que la mano superior no gire demasiado pronto. Luego, mantener el movimiento hasta el final, lo que le ayuda a revertir el movimiento, mantiene bajo el nivel de esfuerzo y, obviamente, le permite mantener el contacto con la pelota durante más tiempo”.
Ohtani acabó con un balance de dos de 13 en la NLDS, registrando dos sencillos en los dos primeros partidos. El cuatro veces MVP intentará superar sus recientes dificultades cuando se enfrente al favorito al premio Cy Young, Jacob Misiorowski, en el primer partido.
Misiorowski ha subido el listón en su segunda temporada en las Grandes Ligas. Pero las dificultades de Ohtani le hicieron bajar a los puestos n.º 5 y 4 de la alineación de los Dodgers para los partidos 3 y 4, respectivamente, frente a los Atlanta Braves.
Sin embargo, la reciente racha negativa de Ohtani no va a cambiar la forma en que Misiorowski le lance.
“Todavía estamos en octubre”, afirmó el as de los Brewers. “Hay que seguir lanzándole como si fuera el mejor del mundo, confiar en tus lanzamientos, vencerle en su propio terreno y hacer tu trabajo”.
Ese historial es en lo que también se apoya el mánager de los Dodgers, Dave Roberts, ya que sigue pronosticando que Ohtani saldrá de su bache.
“En este momento no hay nada en lo que me vaya a basar, simplemente creo en la persona y en su talento”, declaró Roberts en una conferencia telefónica el viernes. “Creo que alejarse un par de días del ambiente de los partidos para trabajar un poco su swing, descansar el cuerpo y la mente es beneficioso. Nunca voy a descartar a Shohei”.
La mayor contribución de Ohtani en la NLDS no tuvo que ver con un swing. En su primer turno al bate del cuarto partido, aprovechó que Tyler Mahle le estaba tratando con cautela y consiguió una base por bolas tras cinco lanzamientos. A continuación, robó la segunda base y aprovechó un par de errores de los Braves para anotar.
“Aparte de [Chris] Sale, creo que hizo un buen trabajo controlando la zona”, dijo Roberts. “He visto algunos swings mejores”.
Pero los Dodgers también se mostraron optimistas mientras Ohtani estaba en la lista de lesionados, y de nuevo tras la semana de descanso que tuvo para trabajar su swing.
“En general, me siento muy bien”, declaró Ohtani el pasado 2 de octubre, la última vez que habló con los medios. “Siento que mi swing está mejor, que fluye con suavidad, y con solo un pequeño ajuste aquí y allá, estaré listo”.
Ohtani no logró forzar una racha positiva en aquel momento. Pero los Dodgers siguen predicando optimismo.
Decisión sobre la plantilla
Roberts afirmó que espera que el jugador de campo Miguel Rojas forme parte de la plantilla de los Dodgers para la NLCS, a pesar de haber sufrido una lesión en la espalda en el tercer partido de la NLDS.
Los Dodgers también tienen previsto incorporar a un lanzador y dar de baja a un jugador de campo, para equilibrar la plantilla con 13 lanzadores y 13 jugadores de campo.
“La duración, contar con un lanzador que pueda aguantar dos o tres entradas, es algo que, en esencia, protege contra los contratiempos en el pitcheo”, dijo Roberts cuando se le preguntó qué priorizarían los Dodgers. “En cuanto a la mano con la que lanzan, están bastante equilibrados. Así que eso realmente no entra en juego. Creo que para nosotros se trata más bien de quién puede cubrir un par de entradas en una situación de presión media o baja”.
El diestro Emmet Sheehan y el zurdo Justin Wrobleski podrían encajar en esa descripción.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have an injury update on veteran infielder Miguel Rojas after he left Game 3 of the National League Division Series early after an errant swing caused major back discomfort. Though he didn't appear in the series-clinching Game 4, manager Dave Roberts still seemed hopeful that last season's World Series hero would be back in time for the the NL Champinship Series rematch against the Milwaukee Brewers.
"I just talked to him briefly, he's in good spirits," Roberts said on Saturday. "We're going to talk to him right now, but as far as the flight, I'm expecting him to be a part of it, be on the roster."
In other news, two-time Cy Young award winner Tarik Skubal opened up about his love for his new team.
The Dodgers acquired Skubal ahead of the trade deadline after he spent the previous six seasons with the Detroit Tigers. With his impending free agency likely pointing towards a contract worth $400 million or more, Dodgers fans should feel more at ease that the southpaw won't look to leave LA before after his most recent comments.
"It's a great team," Skubal said. “The culture that they have here. The preparation, the expectation to win — I love being a part of it."
Finally, Brewers manager Pat Murphy once again has decided to go with the underdog approach ahead of the NLCS. The 103-win Brewers do not appear to be underdogs purely going by regular season records, (or with possessing home field advantage), but the skipper spoke on different "luxuries" that LA has over Milwaukee.
"I just have the front office to thank for being able to pick up the right guys because those type of guys have filled in and did really nicely for us," Muprhy said. "But we don't have the luxury of maybe you have a guy that hadn't pitched much and he's going to make his debut in August. He's a $30 million two-time Cy Young winner or something like that. We don't have that cushion. So we're more desperate to play every single game."

item.title: [New York Post] How the ‘Dinosaur’ Dodgers continue to find the fountain of youth
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: MILWAUKEE –– Dave Roberts delivered the speech. Teoscar Hernández supplied the punch line. In the wake of their National League Division Series defeat of the Atlanta Braves last week, the Dodgers gathered around their manager at the start of a champagne celebration in Truist Park’s visiting clubhouse. First, Roberts extolled their culture and competitiveness. He then declared that “we’re smarter, we’re better and we’re tougher” than their postseason competition. That’s when, from the corner of t
item.content:encoded:
MILWAUKEE –– Dave Roberts delivered the speech. Teoscar Hernández supplied the punch line.
In the wake of their National League Division Series defeat of the Atlanta Braves last week, the Dodgers gathered around their manager at the start of a champagne celebration in Truist Park’s visiting clubhouse.
First, Roberts extolled their culture and competitiveness. He then declared that “we’re smarter, we’re better and we’re tougher” than their postseason competition.
That’s when, from the corner of the room, Hernández chimed in with one more observation.
“And we’re dinosaurs!” he shouted.
Cretaceous creatures, who have once again found the fountain of October youth.
Throughout the regular season and leading into the playoffs, the Dodgers’ aging roster loomed as their biggest area of concern. Their average lineup age of 30.9 years old, according to Baseball Reference, was the oldest in the majors.
Their grizzled veteran core has played more games (and traveled more miles, including two season-opening Asia trips) than any other club in baseball the past two years.
Download The California Post App, follow us on social, and subscribe to our newsletters
California Post News: Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube, WhatsApp, LinkedIn
California Post Sports Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, X
California Post Opinion
California Post Newsletters: Sign up here!
California Post App: Download here!
Home delivery: Sign up here!
Page Six Hollywood: Sign up here!
That’s why the team could help but notice the recent “dinosaur” comment made by new Padres owner José E. Feliciano –– even if he was trying to refer to the actual collection of fossils kept by Dodgers owner Mark Walter.
To the two-time defending champions, it still qualified as a perceived slight.
“We’ve heard it,” 36-year-old third baseman Max Muncy said. “But you can’t focus on the outside stuff for us.
Indeed, the Dodgers do not need any extra motivation this postseason, as they continue their quest for a third-straight World Series title in the NL Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers.
“You worry about yourself,” Muncy said. “You worry about how you’re getting ready for the game, how you’re preparing for the series.”
But talk about their age has nonetheless added some fuel to their competitive fire.
“Los Viejitos!!!” Kiké Hernández captioned on an Instagram photo of him, Muncy, Miguel Rojas, Mookie Betts and Freddie Freeman earlier this week –– playfully using the Spanish term for “old folks” to describe the club’s five eldest statesmen.
“I like our dinosaurs,” Roberts also joked with AM 570 earlier this month. “Our dinosaurs have come through in the biggest spots.”
That was not always the case during the second half of this year’s regular season, when the Dodgers’ offense slipped into such a glaring funk –– highlighted by an inability to consistently slug the ball –– that one rival scout remarked in late August: “This is the oldest they’ve ever looked.”
Since then, however, they have rediscovered a jolt. They scored the fourth-most runs in the majors in September. They outslugged the Braves in the NLDS by belting eight home runs, all but one of which came from players age 33 or older.
Now, they are banking on their experience to give them an edge in this week’s NLCS, starting with a showdown against 24-year-old flamethrowing Brewers ace Jacob Misiorowski in Game 1 on Sunday.
“The toughest part about age is [managing it during the regular] season,” Roberts said. “But once you get through the marathon and you get to the sprint of the postseason, advantage goes to us in the sense of the experience.”
Father Time, of course, will eventually win out at some point.
Even Muncy acknowledged that there has been “some talk” of this being a potential final ride for this version of the roster.
“For us, it’s about playing for each other, and that’s what makes it so special,” Muncy said. “A lot of us have been through a lot of moments together –– good, bad, in the middle –– and I wouldn’t want to share those with anyone else, that’s for sure.”
For now, however, the Dinosaur Dodgers just want to keep on roaring.
Eight wins away from another World Series, age is the least of their concerns.
“I don’t like thinking that this could be towards the end [of our run], because I don’t think it is,” Muncy said. “I think we still have a lot of good baseball left in us. Hopefully we can keep going.”

item.title: [Bozeman Daily Chronicle] Dodgers turn to Tarik Skubal for NLCS Game 1 opener vs Brewers; Yoshinobu Yamamoto set for Game 2
item.dc:creator: BETH HARRIS

The two-time Cy Young Award winner pitched six dominant innings, allowing one run and two hits, in a 5-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves. The left-
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Los Angeles Dodgers will start Tarik Skubal against the Milwaukee Brewers on Sunday in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series.
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, last year's World Series MVP, will start Game 2 on Monday at American Family Field, manager Dave Roberts said Friday.
Skubal also started Game 1 of the NL Division Series. The two-time Cy Young Award winner pitched six dominant innings, allowing one run and two hits, in a 5-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves. The left-hander struck out seven and walked two.
Yamamoto started Game 3 of the NLDS, and struck out 10 over seven innings. The right-hander allowed one run and four hits to go with one walk.
Two-time Cy Young Award winner Blake Snell struggled as the Game 2 starter against the Braves, who won 3-2 to tie the best-of-five series 1-1. The Dodgers went on to eliminate the Braves, 3-1.
Roberts said the Dodgers were in discussions about adding a pitcher for the best-of-seven NLCS, which would require them to drop a position player. Rosters are due Sunday morning.
Miguel Rojas exited Game 3 against the Braves during an at-bat with lower back pain. The utility player underwent imaging, which mostly showed prior back issues. He took ground balls and a couple rounds of batting practice at Dodger Stadium on Friday.
Rojas, 37, has said he's leaning toward retiring at the end of the season.
“Today was encouraging,” Roberts said. “We still have a flight to get on and see how he comes in tomorrow for the workout there, so there’s nothing definitive.”

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers to make playoff roster cut but hope injured World Series hero isn’t it
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris
item.description: The Dodgers are planning to cut a position player from their playoff roster for their upcoming National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers. For now, though, they are hopeful that injured veteran infielder Miguel Rojas won’t have to be the casualty. Rojas remains questionable to be on the Dodgers’ NLCS roster, according to manager Dave Roberts, after he suffered a back injury in Game 3 of the NL Division Series this past week that left him unavailable for the team’s series-c
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers are planning to cut a position player from their playoff roster for their upcoming National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers.
For now, though, they are hopeful that injured veteran infielder Miguel Rojas won’t have to be the casualty.
Rojas remains questionable to be on the Dodgers’ NLCS roster, according to manager Dave Roberts, after he suffered a back injury in Game 3 of the NL Division Series this past week that left him unavailable for the team’s series-clinching victory in Game 4 over the Braves.
However, during a video conference with reporters on Friday, Roberts said Rojas is feeling better and took “a step in the right direction” during a team workout at Dodger Stadium.
“Today was encouraging,” Roberts said. “He took ground balls and took a couple rounds of BP. So that was good to see.”
Roberts emphasized that there is “nothing definitive” yet on Rojas’ status for the best-of-seven matchup against the Brewers, with the team waiting to see how he comes through another workout on Saturday after they travel to Milwaukee ahead of Game 1.
“We’ve just got to be certain that if we do have him on [the roster], he can stay healthy,” Roberts said, wary of the possibility of having to remove Rojas from the roster mid-series because of his injury, which would leave him ineligible for a potential World Series under MLB’s playoff roster rules.
But, Roberts also noted that an MRI revealed no new injury in Rojas’ back — just “stuff that he has had prior history” with — and reiterated that he was “encouraged, again, with what I saw today.”
If Rojas is good to go, then the Dodgers will have to trim another position player from their roster for the NLCS, with the team planning to carry 13 pitchers for the best-of-seven matchup instead of the 12 it had for the five-game divisional round.
The most likely candidate would be Hyeseong Kim, who was called up from Triple-A for the NLDS to serve as a pinch-running and defensive specialist. All the Dodgers’ other reserves (besides unused backup catcher Hunter Feduccia) made important contributions to their NLDS triumph — including rookie sensation Josue De Paula, who drew a pinch-hit walk during Wednesday’s go-ahead seventh-inning rally in Game 4.
As for the extra pitcher the Dodgers could add: Justin Wrobleski, Emmet Sheehan and Jack Dreyer would figure to be the foremost candidates.
“After we get off this call,” Roberts said Friday afternoon, “I’m gonna get with the guys and figure out what arm we’re going to add.”
Rojas initially got hurt while playing second base in Game 3 on Tuesday — in what was his second straight start for the two-time defending champions as an extra right-handed bat in their lineup against an opposing left-handed starter.
He said he tweaked his back while fielding a critical ground ball that got the Dodgers out of a fifth-inning jam, then felt continued discomfort after fouling a pitch off in an eighth-inning at-bat that ultimately forced him out of the game.
Rojas was initially optimistic the issue would be minor, but woke up on the morning of Game 4 feeling “sore and uncomfortable,” preventing him from partaking in any baseball activities that day.
“Tomorrow we will know a little bit more about where my back is,” he said during the team’s clubhouse celebration on Wednesday night. “Looking forward to being able to play in the next series.”
Though Rojas would likely be back in primarily a bench role for the NLCS (the Brewers have just one left-hander in their playoff rotation), his presence is nonetheless important — as a trusted right-handed bat; a defensive option at second base, third base and shortstop; and a steadying veteran presence in his 13th and likely final big-league season.
“We still have a plane flight, there’s another workout, and there’s no deadline right now; we’re not up against it,” Roberts said. “So we have time to ultimately make that decision.”

Rojas hit .267/.312/.391 with four home runs and 23 RBI over 105 games during the regular season.

Throughout his big-league career, Rojas has posted 20.0 bWAR and a .677 OPS with 61 home runs and 386 RBI.

Rojas had the most memorable moment of his career in Game 7 of last year’s World Series when he hit a game-tying home run off Toronto Blue Jays right-hander Jeff Hoffman in the ninth inning.
