item.title: [Sports Gazette] Max Muncy: The Dodgers Unsung Hero - Sports Gazette
item.dc:creator: Conner Rowntree
item.description: Muncy, the longest-tenured Dodger, joined the organization in 2017 on a minor league deal after being cut from the then-Oakland Athletics. The hard-hitting third baseman was called up to the Dodgers in 2018, and in less than a decade, Muncy went from nearly being out of baseball to cementing his legacy as an all-time great. “I remember a guy that just got DFA’d that was sort of kicked to the curb by an organization that didn’t believe in him,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of Muncy. “He was
item.content:encoded:
Muncy, the longest-tenured Dodger, joined the organization in 2017 on a minor league deal after being cut from the then-Oakland Athletics. The hard-hitting third baseman was called up to the Dodgers in 2018, and in less than a decade, Muncy went from nearly being out of baseball to cementing his legacy as an all-time great.
“I remember a guy that just got DFA’d that was sort of kicked to the curb by an organization that didn’t believe in him,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of Muncy. “He was close to being out of baseball … He’s one of the leaders on our ballclub, the longest-tenured Dodger currently. So I just have nothing but praise.”
“The ability to kind of adapt, start, come off the bench and still [do] whatever it takes to help the team win — he’s all-in. He does everything you want as a manager, everything.”
When reflecting on almost being out of the game and facing an early forced retirement in 2016, Muncy broke down.
“Man, there’s a lot with that,” Muncy said. “It’s just a lot.”
Now, nine seasons later, the 36-year-old slugger is a three-time All-Star, Dodger Stadium home run leader, Dodgers playoff home run leader and three-time World Series champion. But “Mad Max” focuses on his team’s success, not personal accolades.
“There’s not much when it comes to me, personally, that I care about,” Muncy said. “But three rings is definitely what I [cherish] most.”
Although Muncy may not focus on his personal statistics, his teammates take notice, not just of the player he is, but the man under the uniform.
“To know that he’s now the Dodger [Stadium] all-time home run leader? Whatever it is … after being an older guy in Triple-A with me and then getting called up … special,” Dodgers reliever Brock Stewart said of Muncy.
“I don’t know if he always believed in himself, and I can relate to that, because I didn’t believe in myself all the time … But to see him and how he persevered through that feeling [or] that self-doubt and became what he is now [is] super special.”
Muncy’s clutch playoff performance has given the Dodgers a chance to win another ring and “Hunt History” by becoming the first National League team to win three consecutive World Series. That role matters even more with Shohei Ohtani slumping. The Dodgers superstar went just 2-for-13 at the plate in the Dodgers NLDS matchup against the Braves. If the Dodgers are going to have any success in the NLCS, especially with the highest-paid and unanimously best baseball player on the planet playing like he’s in pee-wee back in Oshu, Japan, they will need their unsung hero, and Muncy’s teammates know they can rely on him.
“He’s a guy that is always going to show up for the team and do whatever it takes to put the team in a good position,” says Dodger infielder Miguel Rojas.
“He’s a guy you always can root for, especially in this organization full of stars. He always gets [overlooked] a little bit, but I feel like he’s one of the leaders of this club, and he will be until he retires.”
The Dodgers now turn their attention to the MLB’s winningest team this season, the Milwaukee Brewers, and the NLCS. Last year, the Dodgers swept the Brewers en route to their second straight World Series title. This time around, however, the Brewers are confident it will be a different story.
“We’re now as rested as they are,” Brewers owner Mark Attanasio said. “Because last year, we had a very emotional win against the Cubs and a lot of celebrating afterward, and the next day we’re in batting practice. And now we have the same number of days off as they do, and have (Jacob) Misiorowski and (Logan) Henderson and all our pitchers rested.
“So it’s our best against their best, and that’s always fun.”
On the Dodgers side, Manager Dave Roberts gave his club a simple yet clear message after their Game 4, series-clinching win in Atlanta.
“Eight more wins. Stay focused. Everybody in this room helped get us to where we are and where we’re gonna go,” Roberts said to his team in the locker room.
“In the postseason, guys, you don’t know when the moment is gonna come to you. All of us gotta stay focused and get ready.”
If Max Muncy has proven anything during his Dodgers tenure, it’s that he’s ready to do whatever it takes for this team to win and make history. Game 1 of the NLCS is set for Monday in Milwaukee.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers will have time to reset rotation, bullpen, and struggling Shohei Ohtani for NLCS
item.dc:creator: Associated Press
item.description: ATLANTA — Finishing off the Atlanta Braves in four games in the NL Division Series meant more to the Los Angeles Dodgers than avoiding a winner-take-all Game 5. By ending the series with a 4-1 victory, the Dodgers will have extra time to reset their rotation, bullpen and struggling slugger Shohei Ohtani for the Championship Series opening game. "It's important. It was very important," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "Once you get to an elimination game, a Game 5 or a Game 7, anything can happ
item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA — Finishing off the Atlanta Braves in four games in the NL Division Series meant more to the Los Angeles Dodgers than avoiding a winner-take-all Game 5.
By ending the series with a 4-1 victory, the Dodgers will have extra time to reset their rotation, bullpen and struggling slugger Shohei Ohtani for the Championship Series opening game.
"It's important. It was very important," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "Once you get to an elimination game, a Game 5 or a Game 7, anything can happen. And to be able to win today, get back, reset, have a day off tomorrow, set the rotation, it's huge."
The extra rest means Tarik Skubal likely will be the choice to start against Milwaukee instead of handling a Game 5 against the Braves. Similarly, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow will be well rested for their expected NLCS starts.
Infielder Miguel Rojas may need the extra rest for a sore lower back that kept him out.
Also, Edwin Díaz will have ample time to reset after recording saves on back-to-back days to close out the series against Atlanta. The ninth-inning work showed Díaz is re-established as the closer.
"The team trusts me," Díaz said. "I think that was the most important thing for me, the team trusts me. They give me the ball every single day. And the last two nights it's been amazing. That's why I came here to win games and close games like this one. So I'm really happy right now."
Despite those advantages, Roberts is preparing for a tough NLCS as the Dodgers try to move closer to their goal of becoming the first NL team to win three consecutive World Series.
"We've got our work cut out," Roberts said, adding extra rest also will be important for such players as Ohtani and Freddie Freeman.
Ohtani was 2 for 13 against Atlanta and hasn't homered since Aug. 18 while dealing with injuries to his right biceps, left knee and neck that have also kept the two-way player off the mound.
"So kind of enjoy this one, get Shohei a couple of days to get back," Roberts said. "Freddie, he had a big series, but, again a couple of days will help him. Give our guys in the 'pen a little reset. So we'll be ready to go Game 1."
Díaz pitched a perfect ninth inning in the clinching win. The on-field celebration was a low-key affair, but Roberts and his players, wearing "Take October" T-shirts and goggles to protect their eyes, soon were drenched with champagne.
The Dodgers made the most of their opportunity to celebrate another postseason series win while maintaining their focus on a third straight World Series championship.
"Our goal is to win the World Series, not this series," Díaz said. "We've got eight more wins to go. So our goal is win those eight games. And at the end of the day when we win those eight games, we celebrate.
"Now we're going back to LA to keep working. I know all the guys are on the same track. Now we just celebrate a little bit, go back to LA, get working and be ready for Sunday."
Andy Pages' bases-loaded single in the seventh drove in two runs to give the Dodgers a 3-1 lead. Max Muncy added to the lead with a homer in the ninth, his third blast of the postseason.
"Obviously, we have big teams, big series coming up," Pages said. "We're going to face tough teams, so prepare for those moments, but also take advantage of the opportunity of being here and enjoying these moments. And knowing that our ultimate goal is to win the World Series. So focus on that."

item.content:encoded:
Oct 7, 2026, 10:01 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers closer Edwin Diaz picked up his second save in as many nights on Wednesday, pitching a scoreless ninth inning with a strikeout in his team's 4-1 victory over the Atlanta Braves in Game 4 of the National League Division Series. Diaz missed most of the 2026 regular season due to elbow and neck injuries. However, he's been dominant since returning from the injured list in mid-September. Diaz allowed just two baserunners while notching nine strikeouts in his final five innings pitched of the regular season, and he's now logged low-stress saves in each of his first two appearances of the playoffs. With Diaz rounding into form, Los Angeles' bullpen looks like a major strength heading into the National League Championship Series.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
More Recent News
Oct 7, 2026, 9:52 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians left-hander Foster Griffin was dominant in a bulk relief appearance in his team's 9-3 win over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday. Griffin followed Cleveland opener Daniel Espino and allowed two hits and one earned run while striking out seven across 2 2/3 innings of work. The 31-year-old was used exclusively as a starting pitcher during the regular season, posting a 15-6 record with a 3.60 ERA, 1.21 WHIP, and 158 strikeouts across 172 2/3 innings (31 starts) split between the Guardians and the Washington Nationals. However, Griffin struggled mightily late in the year, pitching to a 5.05 ERA in the second half and a 6.87 ERA across 18 1/3 innings in September. If Griffin can rediscover his early-season form in a bullpen role, he could help Cleveland mount a comeback in the ALDS.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:43 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians outfielder Jo Adell had a big night in his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday, going two-for-four with a walk and three RBI. With the game tied 1-1 in the third inning, Adell put the Guardians ahead for good with a three-run triple off of White Sox left-hander Hagen Smith. Across 660 regular-season plate appearances split between the Guardians and the Los Angeles Angels, Adell hit .240/.298/.401 with 23 home runs, 94 RBI, 70 runs scored, and five stolen bases. He was better with Cleveland than he was with Los Angeles, posting a .740 OPS across 204 trips to the plate after the Guardians acquired him at the trade deadline. Adell has notched a couple of key hits for Cleveland in the ALDS and now has four RBI across the first three games of the series.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:32 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Andy Pages had the key hit in his team's 4-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday, logging a go-ahead two-run single off Braves right-hander Robert Suarez in the seventh inning. Pages finished the game with two hits and two RBI in three at-bats. The 25-year-old was a critical piece of the Dodgers lineup during the regular season, hitting .274 with 23 home runs, 85 RBI, 75 runs scored, and 13 stolen bases. However, Pages struggled mightily during the Dodgers' run to the 2025 World Series, notching just four hits in 55 postseason plate appearances. After his big night on Wednesday, Pages has already logged four hits in just 15 plate appearances in the 2026 playoffs.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:19 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians right-hander Cade Smith was lights out to secure his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series on Wednesday. Smith entered the game in the eighth inning and recorded the final six outs, logging five strikeouts without allowing a single baserunner. The 27-year-old was one of the best closers in baseball during the regular season, pitching to a 1.95 ERA and 0.96 WHIP with 107 strikeouts and 41 saves across 74 innings (69 games). Smith has been dominant so far in the Division Series as well, as he's yet to allow a hit or a walk in his four innings of work. If Cleveland is going to mount a comeback in the series, it will likely need Smith to continue his dominance.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 7, 2026, 9:11 PM ET
Cleveland Guardians third baseman Jose Ramirez was one of the stars of his team's 9-3 victory over the Chicago White Sox in Game 3 of the American League Division Series. In five plate appearances, Ramirez recorded a double, a triple, a walk, two RBI, two runs scored, and a stolen base. With Cleveland leading 5-3 in the 8th inning, it was Ramirez's two-run triple that sealed the win for the Guardians and kept the series alive to see Game 4. The 34-year-old battled through injuries and underperformance in 2026, hitting .235/.320/.368 with 12 home runs, 53 RBI, 71 runs scored, and 37 stolen bases across 544 plate appearances. Ramirez also got off to a slow start in the postseason, going hitless in his first eight trips to the plate against the White Sox. If Cleveland is going to rally all the way back from two games down in the ALDS, it will need Ramirez to stay hot in Games 4 and 5.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Robert Gasser Starting Game 4 of NLDS Against Padres


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 8:08 PM ET
Milwaukee Brewers left-hander Robert Gasser will start for the Brewers in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday night at Petco Park against the San Diego Padres, according to Brewers reporter Sophia Minnaert. It will be Gasser's first career postseason start after throwing 2 2/3 innings of relief in the playoffs for the Brew Crew last year. The 27-year-old southpaw went 5-5 on the season with a 3.87 ERA (4.24 FIP) and 1.19 WHIP with a career-high 103 strikeouts and 35 walks in 109 1/3 innings across 21 appearances (20 starts). The problem for Gasser is that he has not made a start in almost two weeks, so he could be a bit rusty. Manager Pat Murphy will surely have a short hook on the young left-hander as the Brewers look to close the best-of-five series out in San Diego. Gasser was outstanding down the stretch in 2026, allowing two earned runs or fewer in each of his last six starts, walking 12 and striking out 31 in 32 1/3 innings during that span. He did not face the Padres at all during the regular season, which could give him a bit of an advantage.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Sophia Minnaert
Mason Miller Back From the Paternity List for Game 4


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 8:03 PM ET
The San Diego Padres announced on Wednesday that they returned right-handed closer Mason Miller from the paternity list, taking the place on the National League Division Series roster of left-handed reliever Wandy Peralta. Miller blew a two-inning save in Game 2 of the series in Milwaukee against the Brewers and was then unavailable for the win in Game 3 at Petco Park on Tuesday night. It is great news for the Padres, who did not have left-handed high-leverage reliever Adrian Morejon on Tuesday due to a left-shoulder issue. The Padres had to go to Game 1 starter, right-hander Michael King, for the two-inning save with both Miller and Morejon unavailable. It is uncertain if Morejon will be able to pitch late in the game in another must-win contest on Wednesday in Game 4, but the Padres will at least have their stud closer back in the fold. The two-time All-Star was lights-out during the regular season, his first full season with the Friars, posting a 1.67 ERA (1.17 FIP), 0.900 WHIP, a career-high and league-high 38 saves, a career-high 129 strikeouts, and 26 walks in just 70 innings pitched. With their season on the line, expect manager Craig Stammen to be aggressive in his usage of Miller if Game 4 is close in the later innings, even though he showed command issues in the ninth on Sunday in Milwaukee.--Keith Hernandez
Source: San Diego Padres
Miguel Rojas Not Worried About Back/Hip Injury


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 12:28 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers veteran infielder Miguel Rojas (back, hip) said he felt some tightness in his left lower-back/hip area during a swing in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday against the hosting Atlanta Braves before he was pulled mid at-bat, according to Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic. However, Rojas was not concerned about his availability for the rest of the series and going forward. Rojas probably will not be in the Dodgers' starting lineup for Game 4 of the series on Wednesday at Truist Park against Braves right-hander Tyler Mahle, but it sounds like he should be available off the bench. The 37-year-old Venezuelan infielder has made two starts so far in the NLDS against the Braves and has gone 1-for-4 with a double and a strikeout. He was hitless in three at-bats with a strikeout in Tuesday's Game 3 win before being replaced at second base by Tommy Edman. Rojas has mostly been a bench player for the Dodgers in his 13th year in the league (fourth with L.A.) in 2026, but he proved in last year's World Series that he is still capable of coming through in the clutch when needed. He hit .267 (60-for-225) with four homers and 23 RBI during the regular season.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Fabian Ardaya
Oct 7, 2026, 11:57 AM ET
St. Louis Cardinals right-handed closer Riley O'Brien was a first-time All-Star in 2026 in his first full season as the team's closer, and he ended the year tied with San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller for the National League lead in saves (38) with a 4.08 ERA across a career-high 64 innings pitched. O'Brien also set a career high in appearances (66) in his first full year as a big-leaguer. He did not allow an earned run in his first 13 appearances of the year and ended the first half with a 3.43 ERA and a 7.9% walk rate in 39 1/3 frames. O'Brien had 24 saves in his first 28 opportunities. But in 27 appearances after the All-Star break, O'Brien had a 5.11 ERA in 24 2/3 innings, and his walk rate rose to 14.4% while he went 14-for-18 in save chances. Three of his blown saves in the second half came in September, and five of his losing decisions came in his final 13 outings. The 31-year-old said he experienced "fatigue" in the closing days of the season and that his legs have "been feeling heavy compared to how they felt early in the year," according to Daniel Guerrero of the St. Louis Post-Dispatch. As he tired, the velocity of O'Brien's pitches suffered. To be able to maintain velocity through the entire season, O'Brien said he plans to focus on putting on "as much muscle as I can."--Keith Hernandez
Source: St. Louis Post-Dispatch - Daniel Guerrero
Curtis Mead the Favorite to Start at Second Base Next Year


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:47 AM ET
Boston Red Sox infielder Curtis Mead is considered the favorite to open next season as the team's starting second baseman, according to Tim Healey of The Boston Globe. The Red Sox acquired Mead from the Washington Nationals at the trade deadline this summer, but he ended up playing in only one game for Boston due to a fractured wrist that he suffered in his second at-bat with the team. The 25-year-old will now have all offseason to heal up, and he will enter spring training as the team's primary option at the keystone as they attempt to get back to the playoffs in 2027. The Australian native was having a breakout 2026 campaign with the Nationals before being traded to Boston, and he finished the year with a .253/.353/.498 slash line with an .851 OPS, 17 home runs, 48 RBI, 49 runs scored, and six stolen bases in 285 at-bats in 88 combined games with Washington and Boston. "That would be, I would say, broadly our plan," said manager Chad Tracy when asked about second base. "He was acquired for a reason. You see the numbers that kind of project at least toward a 30-home run season. And adding that, we were really excited about that."--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Boston Globe - Tim Healey
Walker Buehler to Start Game 4 of NLDS Against Brewers


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:36 AM ET
The San Diego Padres announced that veteran right-hander Walker Buehler will make the start in Game 4 of the National League Division Series on Wednesday night at Petco Park against the visiting Milwaukee Brewers. Buehler will make his first postseason appearance this year after going 9-6 with a 4.63 ERA (4.51 FIP) and 1.35 WHIP with 131 strikeouts and 57 walks in 153 2/3 innings pitched across his 32 starts for the Padres in his first season with the team. The 32-year-old is no longer the high-end ace that he was with the Los Angeles Dodgers, but he does have plenty of postseason experience, posting a 3.04 ERA (3.21 FIP) with 114 strikeouts and 36 walks in 94 2/3 innings pitched. Buehler's last start came on Sept. 26 against the division-rival Arizona Diamondbacks, when he allowed four runs (three earned) with a walk and three strikeouts in just 3 2/3 innings for a no-decision. He picked up a win in his only outing against Milwaukee in 2026, giving up just one earned run with two walks and five strikeouts in six innings at Petco Park back on Aug. 11. Buehler will most definitely be on a short leash in a must-win game for San Diego if he is not on his game early on.--Keith Hernandez
Source: Padres PR
Adrian Morejon Dealing With "Stickiness in his Shoulder"


Keith Hernandez




Oct 7, 2026, 11:28 AM ET
San Diego Padres left-handed reliever Adrian Morejon (shoulder) was unavailable in Game 3 of the National League Division Series at Petco Park on Tuesday night against the Milwaukee Brewers due to "stickiness in his shoulder," manager Craig Stammen told AJ Cassavell of MLB.com. There is still a chance that Morejon will be available for Game 4 against the Brewers in San Diego on Wednesday night as the Friars attempt to force a Game 5 back in Milwaukee on Friday night. With Morejon unavailable and closer Mason Miller on the paternity list, the Padres' bullpen was very short on Tuesday night, but Game 1 starter Michael King came to the rescue and threw the final two innings for SD to pick up a save in the 4-3 victory. Morejon has already had two two-inning appearances in this postseason, once in the Wild-Card Series against the Chicago Cubs and again on Saturday against the Brewers in Game of the NLDS, when he allowed the game-winning home run to catcher William Contreras. The hard-throwing Cuban left-hander was one of the most effective late-inning setup men during the regular season, though, going 9-3 with a 2.83 ERA, 1.08 WHIP, three saves, and a career-high 107 strikeouts in just 86 innings out of the bullpen. With Miller unlikely to be back with the team on Wednesday, the Padres could really use Morejon's left arm on Wednesday evening.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - AJ Cassavell
Oct 6, 2026, 10:58 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers first baseman Freddie Freeman was one of the stars of his team's 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday. Freeman had just one hit in four plate appearances, but it was a solo home run off Braves ace Chris Sale. Freeman put together another strong regular season in 2026, hitting .288/.362/.430 with 16 home runs, 70 RBI, 74 runs scored, and seven stolen bases. The 37-year-old's production tailed off late in the year, as he hit just .184 in September and slugged just one home run across 249 plate appearances after the All-Star break. However, Freeman has looked like his vintage self so far this postseason. Across the first three games of the NLDS, Freeman has logged four hits, two home runs, two RBI, and three runs scored.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 6, 2026, 10:40 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers utility man Enrique Hernandez struck one of the big blows of his team's 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday, clubbing a two-run home run off of Braves ace Chris Sale to open the scoring in the fourth inning. It was Hernandez's only hit of the night, but it helped the Dodgers chase Sale out of the game after just five innings of work. Hernandez missed a large chunk of the regular season with an oblique injury and was not particularly effective when healthy, hitting .222 with four home runs across 96 plate appearances. However, the 35-year-old has a long history as an unlikely postseason hero. Across 332 career plate appearances in the playoffs, Hernandez has now hit .272 with 18 home runs and 44 RBI.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 6, 2026, 10:30 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers right-hander Edwin Diaz notched his first save of the 2026 postseason on Tuesday, shutting the door in his team's 3-1 win over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series. Diaz allowed a leadoff double to Braves second baseman Ozzie Albies but rallied to retire the next three batters he faced. The 2026 regular season was largely lost to injury for Diaz, who spent time on the injured list due to both elbow and neck issues. However, the 32-year-old closed the season strong after returning from the neck injury in mid-September, allowing just one hit and one walk while recording nine strikeouts across his final five innings (five games) of the year. If Diaz can rediscover his peak form in October, he could be an impact arm for the Dodgers at the end of games.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 6, 2026, 10:22 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto was the star of his team's 3-1 victory over the Atlanta Braves in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday night. The 28-year-old allowed just four hits, one walk, and one earned run while recording 10 strikeouts across seven innings of work. Yamamoto was dominant during the regular season, recording a 14-9 record with a 2.53 ERA, 0.87 WHIP, and 182 strikeouts across 185 innings (28 starts). He's also been remarkably effective in the postseason to this point in his career, logging an 8-1 record with a 2.14 ERA, 0.83 WHIP, and 58 strikeouts across 63 innings. Following Yamamoto's gem, the Dodgers will have a chance to close out Atlanta in Game 4 and advance to the National League Championship Series on Wednesday.--Will Brady
Source: ESPN.com
Oct 6, 2026, 10:10 PM ET
San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller has been placed on the paternity list and will not be available for his team's matchup against the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 3 of the National League Division Series on Tuesday, per Kevin Acee of the San Diego Union-Tribune. Miller blew a save opportunity in San Diego's Game 2 loss to the Brewers, allowing a walk-off, two-run single to Milwaukee outfielder Jackson Chourio. Still, the hard-throwing right-hander was one of the best relievers in baseball in the regular season. Across 70 innings (66 games), Miller pitched to a 1.67 ERA and 0.90 WHIP with 129 strikeouts and 38 saves. Without Miller, San Diego left-hander Adrian Morejon could be the next man up in the ninth inning for the Padres.--Will Brady
Source: The San Diego Union-Tribune - Kevin Acee
Miguel Rojas Suffers Back Injury in Game 3 of NLDS


Keith Hernandez




Oct 6, 2026, 8:52 PM ET
Los Angeles Dodgers veteran infielder Miguel Rojas (back) injured himself on a swing in the eighth inning and left Game 3 of the National League Division Series against the Atlanta Braves in the middle of his at-bat on Tuesday night, according to Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic. Rojas was reaching towards his lower back with his left arm after a swing. He was making the start at second base against Braves left-hander Chris Sale, and he went 0-for-3 at the plate with a strikeout before being replaced at the keystone by Tommy Edman. The 37-year-old Venezuelan infielder is a bench player for the Dodgers at this point in his career, but despite not playing all that much anymore, he saved the Dodgers' season in last year's World Series victory over the Toronto Blue Jays in Game 7 of the series. Rojas hit .267 (60-for-225) during the regular season with only four home runs, 23 RBI, 23 runs scored, and a stolen base. If Rojas' injury is serious enough for the Dodgers to remove him from the NLDS roster, he would be unable to return for the NL Championship Series if the team advances.--Keith Hernandez
Source: The Athletic - Fabian Ardaya
Gavin Sheets Scratched From Game 3 Lineup With Neck Stiffness


Keith Hernandez




Oct 6, 2026, 7:44 PM ET
The San Diego Padres announced that outfielder/first baseman Gavin Sheets (neck) was scratched from the Game 3 lineup on Tuesday in the National League Division Series against the visiting Milwaukee Brewers due to neck stiffness. Sheets will be available off the bench, though, so he should be considered day-to-day. Outfielder Samad Taylor is now serving as the designated hitter and will bat eighth in the order against Brewers right-hander Dustin May. Sheets hit 17 homers (two shy of his career high) in 125 regular-season games but missed all of September while on the injured list with a foot injury. The 30-year-old veteran left-handed slugger has played in only two games so far in the postseason for San Diego, but he did have a big two-run home run in Game 2 of the Wild-Card Series against the Chicago Cubs. Since the start of July, Sheets has hit just two home runs, so he has really struggled to tap into his power from the left side in the second half of the season.--Keith Hernandez
Source: San Diego Padres
Ronald Acuna Jr. Battling Knee Soreness, Serving as DH in Game 3


Keith Hernandez




Oct 6, 2026, 4:53 PM ET
Atlanta Braves outfielder Ronald Acuna Jr.'s knee has been sore since he slid during Game 2 of the National League Division Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Sunday, according to Mark Bowman of MLB.com. As a result, Acuna will serve as the designated hitter and bat second for Atlanta in Game 3 of the series in Atlanta against Dodgers right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto. Lane Thomas will now start in right field and bat seventh, with catcher Sean Murphy heading to the bench. Acuna has a history of knee injuries, so the Braves will get him off his feet as the series heads to Atlanta tied one game apiece. The former MVP has gone 2-for-9 with two runs scored and a stolen base at the plate in the first two games of the NLDS against the Dodgers. The Braves will need Acuna to be at his best for the remainder of the series in order to knock off the defending World Series champions. The five-time All-Star had two separate trips to the injured list during the regular season due to hamstring issues and ended up hitting .255/.345/.451 with 20 home runs, 55 RBI, 21 stolen bases, and 61 runs scored across 408 at-bats.--Keith Hernandez
Source: MLB.com - Mark Bowman

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers star Mookie Betts' birthday feat making MLB history proves he's a true champion appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here.
On Wednesday evening, the Los Angeles Dodgers will look to turn out the lights on the Atlanta Braves when the two teams hit the field for Game 4 of their NLDS matchup. The Dodgers climbed back into the driver's seat in this series on Tuesday in a Game 3 win thanks to an epic performance from pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto.
It's been a relatively quiet postseason thus far for Dodgers leadoff hitter Mookie Betts, but perhaps a personal milestone on Wednesday could help change that.
"Today is Mookie Betts' birthday. Birthdays are important. This will be the fourth time he plays a postseason game on his birthday, most in MLB history," reported Sarah Langs of the MLB on X, formerly Twitter.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
Indeed, having a birthday in October means that Betts is no stranger to playing postseason baseball on the special occasion. He turns 34 years old on Wednesday, and has looked like an aging star for most of the series so far against the Braves, not making much happen at the plate.
However, on Wednesday, the Dodgers found a way to get to Braves ace Chris Sale thanks to two straight homers, the second of which was launched by former Atlanta star Freddie Freeman, to put three runs on the board, which was all they needed to get the comfortable win.
The Dodgers now sit just one win away from the NLCS, where they would play either the San Diego Padres or Milwaukee Brewers for the right to go to the World Series.
In any case, Game 4 of Braves vs Dodgers is set to get underway on Wednesday at 6:00 pm ET from Atlanta.
Related: Dodgers' Miguel Rojas not available for Game 4 of NLDS vs. Braves

item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers are back in Atlanta for Game 4 of the NLDS on Wednesday, needing just one more win to clinch the series. After getting to Chris Sale in Game 3, the Dodgers will face right-hander Tyler Mahle, who has turned heads since being acquired at the trade deadline from the San Francisco Giants.
After batting fifth in the starting lineup for the first time as a Dodger, Shohei Ohtani will once again be hitting in the middle third of the order, this time moving up to the cleanup spot with Teoscar Hernández sliding down to the fifth spot in the order.
Max Muncy makes his first start this series since batting 8th in Game 1 against left-hander Dylan Dodd, this time batting sixth in the lineup with Miguel Rojas getting the day off after dealing with back tightness. The hero of Game 3 on offense, Kiké Hernández, makes his second straight start, this time batting seventh while getting the start at second base. Kyle Tucker once again hits in the 8 spot while Andy Pages rounds things out after a multi-hit performance.
Runs have been hard to come by so far this series, as the Dodgers have plated just 10 combined runs over their first three postseason games, all of which have come via home runs. The main Achilles heel for the Dodgers has been their consistent inability to produce with runners in scoring position, as the team is 0-13 in those situations. The Braves, to their credit, have managed to get one hit with runners in scoring position, albeit across 14 at-bats, and have combined to score just eight runs over the first three games.
The Dodgers have fared well in previous matchups against Mahle, as the right-hander has a combined 3-3 record with a 3.15 ERA. Most of the damage came when Mahle was still with the Cincinnati Reds, and in his most recent start against the Dodgers back when he was with San Francisco, he shut them down over seven shutout innings in a 3-0 Giants win on April 22. Since joining Atlanta, Mahle finished the regular season with a 1.99 ERA and limited the Philadelphia Phillies to just one run in his most recent Wild Card start.

item.title: [El Nuevo Día] ¡Boricuas brillan en octubre! Kike Hernández jonronea y Edwin Díaz salva juego en Atlanta
item.dc:creator: Charles Odum

item.content:encoded:
7 de octubre de 2026 - 9:45 PM
Atlanta - Yoshinobu Yamamoto ponchó a 10 bateadores en siete entradas, Enrique “Kike” Hernández conectó un jonrón de dos carreras y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron 3-1 a los Braves de Atlanta el martes por la noche, tomando una ventaja de 2-1 en su Serie Divisional de la Liga Nacional.
Hernández, quien suele brillar en octubre, sacudió su decimoséptimo cuadrangular en postemporada, quebrando un empate con el miembro del Salón de la Fama de Béisbol Carlos Beltrán.
El boricua ahora está empate con Jim Thome, Aaron Judge y David Ortiz en la lista de jonrones en la postemporada.
Yamamoto dominó el muy esperado duelo contra el as de Atlanta, Chris Sale, quien permitió tres carreras y siete imparables en cinco entradas. Yamamoto, Jugador Más Valioso (MVP) de la Serie Mundial de 2025, concedió solo cuatro hits y una base por bolas, mejorando su récord de postemporada a 8-1.
Los Dodgers pueden ganar la serie —pactada al mejor de cinco juegos— y dar un paso más en su intento de convertirse en el primer equipo de la Liga Nacional en ganar tres títulos consecutivos de Serie Mundial si vencen nuevamente a los Braves el miércoles por la noche en el cuarto partido.
Los Braves esperaban que dar descanso adicional a Sale fuera una fórmula ganadora para este crucial tercer encuentro. Sin embargo, tras dejar a seis corredores en base en las primeras tres entradas, permitió el jonrón de dos carreras de Hernández y un cuadrangular solitario de Freddie Freeman en el cuarto episodio.
Ozzie Albies abrió la novena entrada de Atlanta con un doblete contra el muro entre el jardín derecho y el central ante los lanzamientos de Edwin Díaz, avanzando a tercera base tras un rodado de out de Michael Harris II. Díaz dejó al corredor varado cuando Mauricio Dubón fue puesto out en un elevado de foul al jardín derecho y Mike Yastrzemski fue retirado con un rodado al campocorto Mookie Betts.
Tras una temporada agobiado por lesiones, Díaz se apuntó su primer salvado desde el pasado 14 de agosto, cuando lanzó la novena entrada en blanco contra Milwaukee.
FUe además su primer rescate de postemporada desde el 14 de octubre de 2024, cuanto se apuntó un salvamento por los Mets de Nueva York contra los propios Dodgers en la Serie de Campeonato de la Liga Nacional.
Dubón realizó una atrapada saltando sobre la barda del jardín izquierdo para robarle un jonrón a Freeman en la tercera entrada; sin embargo, Freeman logró conectar su cuadrangular una entrada más tarde. El jonrón de Hernández hacia el jardín izquierdo impulsó a Andy Pages, quien había conectado un sencillo. Un out después, Freeman conectó el jonrón número 18 de su carrera en postemporada hacia el jardín derecho, ampliando la ventaja a 3-0.
El mánager de los Dodgers, Dave Roberts, bajó al bateador designado Shohei Ohtani al quinto puesto del orden al bate, debido a que Ohtani registraba un promedio de 3 de 15 en su carrera contra Sale. Ohtani se había ido de 4-0 con dos ponches ante Sale cuando los Dodgers perdieron 1-0 el 26 de agosto en Atlanta. Roberts predijo acertadamente que Ohtani tendría oportunidades con corredores en base al batear en una posición más baja del orden de bateo.
En la primera entrada, con corredores en primera y segunda, Sale ponchó a Ohtani para cerrar el episodio. En la tercera, con dos corredores en base, Ohtani llegó a primera gracias a una interferencia del receptor Drake Baldwin —lo que llenó las bases—, antes de que Miguel Rojas terminara la entrada con un elevado al jardín derecho. Ohtani recibió una base por bolas al abrir la octava entrada frente a Brent Suter, el cuarto lanzador de Atlanta.
Un rodado de Baldwin a primera base, con las bases llenas, impulsó a Dubón —quien había conectado un sencillo— en la quinta entrada, anotando así la única carrera de Atlanta ante Yamamoto.
Rojas abandonó el partido durante un turno al bate en la octava entrada. El segunda base pareció lastimarse la espalda al realizar un swing y fue sustituido por Tommy Edman. Los Dodgers informaron que la lesión consistía en dolor en la zona lumbar.
Tanner Scott sumó dos ponches en una octava entrada sin anotaciones para Los Ángeles.
Las noticias explicadas de forma sencilla y directa para entender lo más importante del día.

item.title: [WSLS] Yamamoto is dominant again as Dodgers ride homers from Hernández and Freeman to 3-1 win over Braves
item.dc:creator: Charles Odum; Associated Press
item.description: ATLANTA – Yoshinobu Yamamoto felt trust from Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts when he remained in a crucial NL Division Series game after a stressful fifth inning. “I’d like to continue living up to the highest expectation,” Yamamoto said through a translator. Recommended Videos The right-hander from Japan continues to do more than just meet expectations in the postseason. Yamamoto struck out 10 in seven brilliant innings, Kiké Hernández hit a two-run homer and the Dodgers beat the Atlan
item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA – Yoshinobu Yamamoto felt trust from Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts when he remained in a crucial NL Division Series game after a stressful fifth inning.
“I’d like to continue living up to the highest expectation,” Yamamoto said through a translator.
Recommended Videos
The right-hander from Japan continues to do more than just meet expectations in the postseason.
Yamamoto struck out 10 in seven brilliant innings, Kiké Hernández hit a two-run homer and the Dodgers beat the Atlanta Braves 3-1 on Tuesday night to take a 2-1 lead in their NL Division Series.
Yamamoto dominated his much-anticipated matchup with Atlanta ace Chris Sale, who allowed three runs and seven hits in five innings. Last year's World Series MVP permitted only four hits and one walk while improving to 8-1 with a 2.14 ERA in 11 career postseason outings, including 10 starts.
His 10 strikeouts were a postseason high for him.
“I was confident and able to control all my pitches today,” Yamamoto said.
The Dodgers can clinch the best-of-five series and take another step toward becoming the first National League team to win three consecutive World Series by beating the Braves again Wednesday night in Game 4.
Atlanta hoped giving Sale extra rest would be a winning formula in the pivotal third game. Instead, after stranding six runners in the first three innings, he gave up the two-run homer to Hernández and a solo shot to former Braves star Freddie Freeman in the fourth.
“He was still touching 100 (mph),” manager Walt Weiss said of Sale. “The stuff was fine. Like I said, maybe the command not perfect. It wasn’t bad. But they did a nice job against him.”
That was all the offensive support Yamamoto and relievers Tanner Scott and Edwin Díaz would need.
Ozzie Albies opened the Atlanta ninth with a double off the right-center wall against Díaz and moved to third on Michael Harris II's groundout. Díaz stranded the runner and earned a save when Mauricio Dubón fouled out to right field and Mike Yastrzemski grounded out to shortstop Mookie Betts.
A homer for the boo birds
Freeman said he didn't mind being booed by Atlanta fans in the sellout crowd of 42,420.
“I’ve got a gray uniform on,” Freeman said. “I expect boos. It’s OK. ... It’s all love. I still love everybody here and I’m looking forward to tomorrow.”
Dubón made a leaping catch over the left-field wall to rob Freeman of a home run in the third. Freeman wouldn't be denied an inning later. Hernández's homer to left drove in Andy Pages, who singled. One out later, Freeman pulled his 18th career postseason homer to right field for a 3-0 lead.
Lineup change
Roberts moved designated hitter Shohei Ohtani down to No. 5 in the lineup because Ohtani was 3 for 15 in his career against Sale. Ohtani went 0 for 4 with two strikeouts against Sale when the Dodgers lost 1-0 on Aug. 26 in Atlanta.
Roberts correctly predicted Ohtani would have opportunities with runners on base hitting lower in the order.
With runners on first and second in the first, Sale struck out Ohtani to end the inning. With two runners on base in the third, Ohtani reached on catcher's interference by Drake Baldwin to load the bases before Miguel Rojas ended the inning with a flyball to right field. Ohtani walked to lead off the eighth against Brent Suter, Atlanta's fourth pitcher.
Baldwin's bases-loaded grounder to first base drove in Dubón, who singled, in the fifth for Atlanta's only run.
Injury report
Rojas left during an at-bat in the eighth. The second baseman appeared to injure his back on a swing and was replaced by Tommy Edman. The Dodgers announced the injury as lower back pain.
Roberts said Rojas probably won't start on Wednesday and his availability off the bench will be determined before the game.
“I give him credit for conceding that at-bat,” Roberts said.
Weiss made a late change, moving Ronald Acuña Jr. from right field to designated hitter. Weiss said Acuña jammed his knee on a slide in Game 2. Acuña remained in the game but the knee was sore on Tuesday, leading to the lineup change.
Milestone win for Roberts
Roberts now has 71 career postseason wins, tying Tony La Russa for second-most in major league history. Joe Torre is first with 84.
Up next
Braves right-hander Tyler Mahle is expected to face Dodgers right-hander Tyler Glasnow in Game 4 on Wednesday night. Mahle said Tuesday an abdominal pull is now a “non-issue.” He felt the pull before allowing one run in seven innings of a 4-3 loss to Philadelphia in 10 innings during the NL Wild Card Series last week.
___

item.title: [MLB.com] Dubón le niega un jonrón a Freeman... pero Freddie cobra revancha después
item.dc:creator: Paul Casella
item.description: Después de que Sale consiguiera cada uno de sus primeros seis outs por la vía del ponche en el Juego 3 de la SDLN contra los Dodgers, Dubón registró el primer out defensivo y lo hizo de manera espectacular. Con un corredor en primera y nadie fuera en la parte alta del tercer inning, la exsuperestrella de los Bravos Freddie Freeman conectó un batazo profundo hacia el jardín izquierdo que salió de su bate a 101.3 mph. Dubón siguió la trayectoria de la pelota hasta la pared y calculó perfectamente
item.content:encoded:
Después de que Sale consiguiera cada uno de sus primeros seis outs por la vía del ponche en el Juego 3 de la SDLN contra los Dodgers, Dubón registró el primer out defensivo y lo hizo de manera espectacular.
Con un corredor en primera y nadie fuera en la parte alta del tercer inning, la exsuperestrella de los Bravos Freddie Freeman conectó un batazo profundo hacia el jardín izquierdo que salió de su bate a 101.3 mph. Dubón siguió la trayectoria de la pelota hasta la pared y calculó perfectamente su salto para realizar la atrapada justo frente a un grupo de relevistas de los Dodgers, quienes se preparaban para que la bola cayera en el bullpen de los visitantes.
La atrapada de Dubón probablemente le robó un posible jonrón de dos carreras a Freeman, pero como mínimo evitó un extrabase y, casi con toda seguridad, una carrera o dos en el episodio.
Los Dodgers llenaron las bases gracias a un sencillo de Will Smith con dos outs y a que Shohei Ohtani llegó a salvo por interferencia del receptor, pero Sale salió ileso al hacer que Miguel Rojas conectara una línea al jardín derecho para terminar la entrada.
Antes de siquiera necesitar la ayuda de su defensa, Sale se unió a Mike Hampton (Juego 2 de la SDLN del 2003) como los únicos lanzadores de los Bravos en conseguir cada uno de sus primeros seis outs por la vía del ponche en un juego de postemporada.
Freeman se desquitó en su siguiente turno al bate, cuando disparó con autoridad un cuadrangular hacia el jardín derecho-central, el 18vo vuelacercas de su carrera en postemporada, para darle a los Dodgers una ventaja de 3-0.

item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
ATLANTA — The Dodgers went into Game 3 of the National League Division Series knowing they couldn’t be so reliant on the home run, especially with Braves ace Chris Sale on the mound. And yet, in a 3-1 win, it was the home run ball, paired with a masterful performance on the mound from right-hander Yoshinobu Yamamoto, that secured the victory.
The Dodgers pulled ahead to a 2-1 lead in the best-of-five series.
The Dodgers tried to score in other ways, putting on six baserunners in the first three innings of the game. But it didn’t work.
They failed to take advantage of some luck and poor defense from the Braves in the first inning, as Mookie Betts beat out a soft ground ball up the first base line and Teoscar Hernández reached on a fielding error by Braves shortstop Ha-Seong Kim.
Yoshinobu gives up four hits and strikes out 10 and Kiké Hernández hits a two-run home run to power the Dodgers to victory in Game 3 of the NLDS.
The lineup shuffling manager Dave Roberts did against Sale had superstar Shohei Ohtani, batting fifth, walking up to the plate with two outs and runners on first and second. His over-anxious approach at the plate so far this postseason followed him into the at-bat. And he struck out whiffing on a slider in the opposite batter’s box.
The next inning, Kyle Tucker hit a two-out single into left, baited Sale into picking over to first base twice, and then stole second. But he was stranded there, as Kiké Hernández went down swinging. All six of the Dodgers’ outs in the first two innings came via the strikeout.
In the third, the Dodgers loaded the bases. Mookie Betts started the effort with a double through the left side of the infield. And it looked for a moment as if Freddie Freeman had capitalized on the opportunity with a runner in scoring position.
He stayed back on a fastball and crushed it to deep left field, on a trajectory to just clear the short fence. But Braves left fielder Mauricio Dubón made a leaping catch, holding into the ball as he slammed into the wall.
Undeterred, the Dodgers kept putting runners on base. With two outs, Will Smith stayed through a slider to single. Ohtani clipped Braves catcher Drake Baldwin’s mitt and was awarded first base for catcher’s interference. Then Miguel Rojas, who’d exit the game in the eighth inning mid-at-bat with what the Dodgers called low back pain, hit a line drive that found leather to end the inning.
So, back to the long ball.
Perennial postseason hero Kiké Hernández delivered the first blow. With Andy Pages on first, after his first hit of the series, Hernández launched a changeup into the left-field stands. Then, two batters later, Freeman turned on an inside sinker and sent it over the right-field fence — where Dubón had no chance to track it down.
Game 3 was billed as a matchup between aces: Sale, whom the Braves tabbed for Tuesday because of his workload in their wild-card series, and Yamamoto, whom the Dodgers partially held back for the first two games with the NLCS in mind.
Yamamoto held up his end of the bargain, limiting the Braves to four hits and one run in seven innings.
He retired 10 of the first 11 batters he faced. The only baserunner in that time, Michael Harris II, bunted for a single. Yamamoto crashed hard, slipping on the slick grass as he tried to pivot but still managing to make a throw to first from the ground.
Shohei Ohtani is batting fifth in the lineup against Braves ace Chris Sale in Game 3 of the NLDS. He hasn’t hit fifth or lower in a starting lineup since 2020 with the Angels.
He only wavered in the fifth, loading the bases with a pair of singles and a four-pitch walk. The Braves’ batting order turned over, and Yamamoto got Baldwin to ground out to first, but that allowed a run. Then he induced Ronald Acuña Jr. to ground out to second to escape the jam. Rojas ranged to his left to field the ball and made an on-target throw even as he slipped on the grass in shallow right field.
Yamamoto didn’t allow another baserunner.
Left-handed reliever Tanner Scott served as the Dodgers’ setup man, throwing a hitless eighth. And right-hander Edwin Díaz came in for his first save opportunity since Aug. 14 against the Brewers.
He gave up a double off the wall to Ozzie Albies to open the inning but retired the next three batters.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers World Series hero Miguel Rojas exits after experiencing discomfort
item.dc:creator: Thomas L Murray
item.description: During the eighth inning of Game 3 of the NLDS on Tuesday, Dodgers middle infielder Miguel Rojas exited the game. item.content:encoded:
During the eighth inning of Game 3 of the NLDS on Tuesday, Dodgers middle infielder Miguel Rojas exited the game.
Rojas was seen in visible discomfort after fouling off a fastball from Braves reliever Brent Suter.
Rojas started limping back toward the batter’s box and was immediately evaluated by a member of the Dodgers’ training staff and manager Dave Roberts.
Shortly after the injury, the Dodgers announced that Rojas was removed from the game due to lower back pain.
Tommy Edman replaced Rojas at second base.
Rojas went 0-for-3 before departing Tuesday. He has one hit in the series — a double in Saturday’s 5-3 victory.
Rojas is expected to retire after the season is over.
Rojas was a World Series hero last year after hitting a game-tying home run in Game 7 against the Blue Jays, sending the game to extra innings.
The Dodgers went on to win the game in the 11th when Will Smith hit a go-ahead home run.
In Tuesday’s game, the Dodgers’ offense popped off in the fourth inning, when Kiké Hernández and Freddie Freeman homered to give LA a 3-0 lead.
The Braves scored in the fifth when Drake Baldwin grounded out to first after Dodgers starting pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto loaded the bases.
Yamamoto finished with a career-high 10 strikeouts. He tossed 98 pitches in seven innings, giving up four hits, one run and one walk.

item.content:encoded:
Miguel Rojas was the hero for the Los Angeles Dodgers during the 2025 postseason, but his 2026 postseason is off to a much worse start.
The Dodgers infielder Rojas had to exit Tuesday’s NLDS Game 3 against the Atlanta Braves in the middle of an at-bat. During the eighth inning at Truist Park in Atlanta, Ga., Rojas fouled off a 1-0 pitch from Braves reliever Brent Suter and immediately came up grimacing.
Rojas was unable to finish his plate appearance and went on to walk off the field with trainers. Here is the video of Rojas’ injury.
Miguel Rojas exits the game after he appears to have injured his back on a swing https://t.co/Rmc25l0OkW
— Talkin’ Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) October 7, 2026
Dodgers teammate Tommy Edman replaced Rojas in the game, finishing out his at-bat and also taking Rojas’ place in the field. The Dodgers soon officially announced that Rojas had left the contest due to “low back pain.”
Now 37 years old, Rojas is a two-time Dodgers champion who is very beloved by the team’s fanbase. Most notably, Rojas was directly responsible for the Dodgers’ 2025 championship by famously hitting a game-tying ninth-inning home run in Game 7 of the World Series against the Toronto Blue Jays.
But Rojas is now only on a one-year deal with the Dodgers and previously announced that he intends for the 2026 season to be his last. As such, it remains to be seen if that was Rojas’ last-ever at-bat in Major League Baseball.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have had plenty of postseason heroes during their World Series runs in 2024 and 2025.
Last year, the biggest may have been backup infielder Miguel Rojas, who hit a game-tying home run in Game 7 against the Toronto Blue Jays in the ninth inning.
As a result, Rojas has continued to get opportunities in 2026 and was inserted into the starting lineup for Game 3 against the Atlanta Braves in this year's NLDS. He also started Game 2 in place of Max Muncy at third base.
Oct 6, 2026; Cumberland, Georgia, USA; ]Los Angeles Dodgers second baseman Miguel Rojas (72) throws to first base for an out against the Atlanta Braves during the first inning in game three of the NLDS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at Truist Park. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
Rojas was put in to hit against Braves left-hander Chris Sale given his platoon advantage as a right-handed hitter. It did not work out through his first three at-bats as he went 0-for-3 with a strikeout.
Rojas remained in the game for a fourth at-bat in the eighth inning against Braves reliever Brent Suter, who is also a southpaw.
Unfortunately, he did not finish the at-bat. After fouling off the second pitch he immediately reached for his lower back with his left arm.
A trainer came out to visit Rojas and after a brief discussion he was removed from the game with Tommy Edman taking over mid at-bat. Edman popped up shortly after. The Dodgers released an update shortly after. "Miguel Rojas left tonight's game with low back pain," the team wrote on X.
Latest Update on Miguel Rojas
During the broadcast, Ken Rosenthal of The Athletic reported that Rojas originally suffered the setback while fielding a ground ball back in the 5th inning.
If Rojas' injury is serious enough to keep him out for the remainder of the NLDS, the Dodgers would have to replace him on the roster.
That would also keep him out of the NLCS should Los Angeles advance, which would be a huge loss given the postseason experience he brings.

He was replaced by Tommy Edman, who popped out on the first pitch he saw. Rojas drew the start with the left-handed Chris Sale on the mound. It was his second consecutive start after he got the nod in Ga
item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers infielder Miguel Rojas has exited Game 3 of the National League Division Series in the top of the eighth inning with an injury.
Rojas appeared to tweak his lower back on a swing and is now out of the game. He initially tweaked his back on a defensive play earlier in the game.
He was replaced by Tommy Edman, who popped out on the first pitch he saw.
Rojas drew the start with the left-handed Chris Sale on the mound. It was his second consecutive start after he got the nod in Game 2 with the lefty Ray Kerr starting.
After going 1-for-1 against Kerr before being replaced by Max Muncy, Rojas was 0-for-3 on Tuesday.
What is Miguel Rojas' Injury?
The Dodgers announced Rojas exited the game with low back pain.
Is Miguel Rojas Retiring After This Season?
Rojas is in the midst of what's expected to be his final season in Major League Baseball. The 37-year-old entered the year saying this would be his last. However, he then left the door open for a potential return in 2027 if the Dodgers won the World Series this year.
Before Tuesday's game, Rojas spoke to reporters and still didn't have a firm answer.
"I'm not thinking about that at all. I'm not thinking about my future or anything," Rojas said. "In regards to my retirement or stepping away from the game, I will never think about stepping away from the game because of my performance or my way to play my game. I think there's other things in life that I'm contemplating about that decision. But if I have to tell you right now, I'm not 100% like [Clayton] Kershaw was last year or others in the past that knew for sure they want to go after this year.
"For me it's more, I would say it's a 40/60 right now that I want to stay in the game and I want to play. But it's not about me. It's about the organization. It's about doing what we're supposed to do to help the team win this year. And then after that we will have conversations."
Rojas, who hit the game-tying home run in Game 7 of the 2025 World Series against the Toronto Blue Jays, had a strong season in 2026, appearing in 105 games and hitting .267 with and OPS of .703. He's still an elite defender in the infield.
Off the field, he's a leader in the Dodgers clubhouse.
Manager Dave Roberts will have an update on his veteran after the game.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts named potential players who could get a spot in the starting lineup for NLDS Game 3.
The Dodgers' offense hasn't been its best through the first two games of the series, relying exclusively on homers to score all seven of their runs so far. A change of personnel could help the Dodgers string together some hits and bring some more runs across.
Ahead of Tuesday's matchup, Roberts named three players who could insert themselves into the lineup for NLDS Game 3.
"You've got Kiké [Hernandez], you've got [Miguel Rojas], you've got Muncy," Roberts said.
Hernandez provides plenty of positional versatility for the Dodgers, and could stand in at a number of positions if the Dodgers want to approach their matchup against the left-handed Chris Sale with a lineup full of right-handed batters.
The fan favorite's most likely role if he were to start Game 3 would be as the third baseman, keeping left-handed third baseman Max Muncy out of the lineup for a second consecutive game despite hitting homers in each of the first two games of the series, but he could also play either of the corner outfield spots if needed.
Rojas would stand in at second base for Tommy Edman in the most likely case, as Roberts isn't quite ready to move Edman into center to replace Andy Pages despite his rough postseason record.
Who Won't Start for the Dodgers on Tuesday?
In addition to those three players, Roberts revealed Josue De Paula won't have a starting spot against Sale.
"Josue De Paula I don't see being an option," Roberts said.
As a left-handed batter, De Paula's omission from the lineup makes plenty of sense, and he will be available off of the bench for the remainder of the game.
Other than De Paula, Hyeseong Kim and Hunter Feduccia almost certainly won't start, but the rest of the lineup could change as the Dodgers look to find a spark in their offense. With the series tied at one game apiece, the Dodgers need to claim victory in one of their two games in Atlanta to ensure they return home for a game if necessary.
Game 3 could swing momentum in the Dodgers' direction, and they'll do anything to take the lead in the NLDS. Tuesday's game begins at 3:00 p.m. PT.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dave Roberts Ponders Dodger Lineup Tweaks Ahead of Game 3

The Dodgers manager said he is considering lineup tweaks against Chris Sale, including the possibility of moving Shohei Ohtani lower in the order. He also made it clear that Edwin Díaz has worked his way back into serious ninth-inning consideration after his sharp outing in Game 2. item.content:encoded:
ATLANTA, GA — Dave Roberts spent Monday weighing changes on both sides of the ball before Game 3 in Atlanta.
The Dodgers manager said he is considering lineup tweaks against Chris Sale, including the possibility of moving Shohei Ohtani lower in the order. He also made it clear that Edwin Díaz has worked his way back into serious ninth-inning consideration after his sharp outing in Game 2.
With the NLDS tied 1-1, Roberts sounded open to adjusting quickly.
Díaz Could Close
“I think that we’ve built him up, regained the confidence in him and himself,” Roberts said of Díaz. “I think that it’s certainly a viable option for tomorrow night. I feel very confident with him finishing a game.”
Roberts said Díaz’s most recent outing was about as good as he has seen from him.
“That last outing was as good as we’ve seen him throw, and it’s hard to imagine throwing any better,” Roberts said. “He’s put himself in a position to be the closer.
“In October, I don’t pay too much attention to the long sample of a season in a lot of cases, because in October things happen quickly and you’ve got to be willing to read and react.”
Roberts also praised the way Díaz handled a difficult season.
“Character,” he said. “That’s the main thing. When things aren’t going the best and how players respond, that’s telling.
“The way he stayed the course, dealt with the injuries, went to OKC on a longer rehab to work things out and then took on whatever role we had for him says a lot about him.”
Lineup Changes Are on the Table
Roberts also acknowledged that the Dodgers could look different against Sale.
“I am considering it,” he said. “I think that’s a very fair question. I have to be mindful of it being two games, and then within those two games, what have I seen? Are we seeing good at-bats?”
He pointed to Will Smith as someone whose results have not matched the quality of his plate appearances.
“I think Will Smith is taking good at-bats, just missing some pitches, taking good swings, not chasing much,” Roberts said. “Versus other people maybe expanding, trying to do too much.
“Those are things that you’re trying to make bets on. Then you’re looking at tomorrow with Sale, the history, recency, how guys are prepared and will prepare for Sale. So yeah, I’m thinking through that, and there are possible changes.”
Roberts listed Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas and Max Muncy among the options he could work into the lineup.
“At the end of the day, our guys are our guys,” he said. “I can tweak a lineup. I can insert, take out a player or two, but we still have to go out there and play, execute and take good at-bats.”
Moving Ohtani Is Possible
Roberts said he would consider moving Ohtani further down in the order if he believes it helps the team.
“I would,” he said. “I think moving him from one to two, but going further than that, I’m open to it.
“If I do, I would obviously have the conversation with Shohei to explain why. At the end of the day, every conversation I’ve had with him is whatever is best for the team, he’s all in on. I know that undoubtedly.”
Roberts thinks some of Ohtani’s recent issues have come from trying to do too much.
“I think there’s a little bit of trying to do too much,” he said. “Everything orbits around Shohei in the sense of his talent, and the Braves are going to enter with caution. They’re going to continue to expand as long as we keep giving that to them.
“Until we show some discipline, they’re going to continue to use that playbook.”
He also said Ohtani may be pressing for power.
“Hitting homers, slugging is so much a part of his hallmark in the batter’s box,” Roberts said. “He’s very in tune with what’s being said, what he hasn’t done.
“But that base hit the other way yesterday, that’s production. Against a guy like Chris Sale, that gives you a chance. Trying to chase slug tomorrow night might not be the right plan given the starter.”
Roberts Still Believes in Pages
Andy Pages has also struggled, but Roberts said he plans to keep giving him chances.
“I’m going to continue to give Andy leash,” Roberts said. “I believe in him. I feel that for us to win the World Series this year, we’re going to need him to be an active part of our team.
“This is, for me, given how he has come into the postseason, too small of a sample. He has taken two walks. Tomorrow is not going to be the end-all, be-all because Sale is a tough matchup, but I still want to see good at-bats.”
Roberts believes the main issue is pressing.
“I think there’s trying to do too much,” he said. “When he came back, he was swinging the bat really well, had success, and now I think there’s a little bit of trying too much.”
Freeman Looks Healthier
One hitter Roberts feels especially good about is Freddie Freeman.
“I think he’s gotten into his legs a lot more,” Roberts said. “He’s moving balls in the hitting zone forward. He’s as healthy as he’s been in quite some time. I think the mechanics are sound.”
Roberts credited the five-day break with helping Freeman get his knee into better shape.
“The week off was really crucial for him,” he said. “Being able to manage that with the five days off got him back to health to be able to work through some things without having to perform in a game setting.”
Sale vs. Yamamoto
Roberts expects Sale to attack the Dodgers much the same way he did when Atlanta faced them in August.
“The fastball just sort of bullied us at the top of the zone,” Roberts said. “There was some chase down below, and with the lefties, throwing more two-seamers to keep us honest in and then expand away.”
Still, Roberts believes the Dodgers are in a better offensive place than they were then.
“I do think we are in a different spot,” he said. “The stakes are certainly higher. There is familiarity on both sides. I think we’ll see better at-bats.
“Chris is going to be tough regardless. We know that. We know we’re going to be in for a dogfight, but I just don’t see him bullying us like he did his last start.”
And Roberts feels good about the pitcher the Dodgers will send out against him.
“There should be a lot of talk about Chris Sale, but our guy’s pretty dang good,” Roberts said. “He’s been a very good pitcher in the postseason, so we feel very good about that.
“I think both pitchers are going to pitch well. It’s kind of who grinds out at-bats best.”

A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.title: [New York Post] Dodgers World Series hero Miguel Rojas earns US citizenship: ‘I’m really proud of being an American’
item.dc:creator: Thomas L Murray
item.description: As Miguel Rojas is entering the final chapter of a 13-year career, he has a lot to be proud of. One thing that he is certainly proud of happened over the Dodgers’ bye week last week, when he revealed he flew out to Miami to take his citizenship test and passed. “As soon as I made the decision that I wanted to do this, I wanted to do it for my family, for my kids and for the future of them,” Rojas said. “So I’m really proud of being an American.” Rojas, 37, first came to America after he arrived
item.content:encoded:
As Miguel Rojas is entering the final chapter of a 13-year career, he has a lot to be proud of.
One thing that he is certainly proud of happened over the Dodgers’ bye week last week, when he revealed he flew out to Miami to take his citizenship test and passed.
“As soon as I made the decision that I wanted to do this, I wanted to do it for my family, for my kids and for the future of them,” Rojas said. “So I’m really proud of being an American.”
Rojas, 37, first came to America after he arrived as a 16-year-old prospect out of Venezuela with the Cincinnati Reds.
Since then, he’s developed a whole life in the United States, and he and his wife, Marianna Rojas Gamboa have two children that were born here when he was playing with the Miami Marlins.
“I’m proud of being working here for over 20 years now,” Rojas said. “I’ve been playing professional baseball now for a long time, and that gave me the opportunity to learn the culture, the country, and I don’t take that for granted.”
On the baseball field, Rojas has had a lot to celebrate as he is a two-time World Series champion with the Dodgers.
For Rojas, Dodgers fans will always remember him as a World Series hero last year, when he had a game-tying home run in the ninth inning against Toronto Blue Jays closer Jeff Hoffman to even the score at four apiece.
The Dodgers would get the win after Will Smith made World Series history by hitting the first Game 7 extra-innings go-ahead home run.
While the Dodgers are preparing to play Game 3 of the NLDS on Tuesday against the Atlanta Braves, Rojas’ time on the baseball field will soon be coming to an end, as he announced at the beginning of the season that he plans to retire after the season.
In his 13-year career in the MLB, Rojas has played five seasons with the Dodgers and has a career 19.6 WAR, a .260 batting average, 61 home runs and 386 RBIs.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have faced two bullpen games to kick off their National League Division Series battle with the Atlanta Braves.
On Tuesday, things will get much more difficult.
The Dodgers are going up against 10-time All-Star and former Cy Young award winner Chris Sale. The left-hander is coming off a regular season in which he had a 2.16 ERA and 200 strikeouts over 162.2 innings. He then allowed three runs over 6.1 innings in his wild-card Game 1 start, and pitched 1.1 scoreless innings to close out Game 3.
The Dodgers know what they're up against with Sale, one of baseball's best pitchers.
"Chris is going to be tough," Roberts said. "We know we're going to be in for a dogfight."
The difficult lefty matchup also has manager Dave Roberts considering some lineup changes.
“I think so," Roberts said. "I am considering it. I think that’s a very fair question. I think that I have to be mindful of — it’s two games, and then with the two games, what have I seen?”
Roberts mentioned Enrique Hernandez and Miguel Rojas as potential options to be in the lineup. The only Dodgers with any semblance of success against Sale in their careers are Mookie Betts (7-for-18) and Freddie Freeman (5-for-16).
The Dodgers have been especially reliant on the home run this series, with all seven of their runs coming via the long ball.
In Sunday's Game 2, they went 0-for-8 with runners in scoring position.
Sale faced the Dodgers on Aug. 27, firing a complete-game shutout with 11 strikeouts and just five hits allowed.
Dave Roberts Considering Moving Shohei Ohtani Down in the Lineup
The Dodgers have plenty of players struggling in the lineup, including Will Smith (0-for-8), Andy Pages (0-for-7) and Tommy Edman (0-for-5).
At the top of the lineup, however, is Shohei Ohtani, who is 2-for-8 with two singles and two strikeouts. He's looked far from his usual self.
"I think there's, like we've talked about, he's not 100%," Roberts said on Monday. "But at the end of the day, he can still do a better job of staying in the strike zone. ... I think that's something that — it's hard to have success when you're out of the zone. ... And Shohei understands, any hitter understands that. So I think that's the thing is — then the question is how do we get him into it? I think there's a little bit of trying to do too much. I think that's a piece."
Roberts said he's open to moving Ohtani down in the lineup, especially with the tough left-hander on the mound.
However, he wouldn't commit to anything on Monday.
"Going further than [No. 2]? I'm open to it," Roberts said. "It's something that, if I do, I would obviously have the conversation with Shohei to explain why. And at the end of the day, every conversation I've had with him is, whatever is best for the team, he's all in on.”
For what it's worth, Ohtani is 3-for-15 against Sale in his career with five strikeouts.
"At the end of the day, our guys are our guys," Roberts said. "And, yeah, I can tweak a lineup. I can kind of insert, take out a player or two. But at the end of the day we still have got to go out there and play and execute and take good at-bats."

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Move Shohei Ohtani down in the Dodgers' lineup? Dave Roberts is 'open' to it

item.content:encoded:
Move Shohei Ohtani down in the Dodgers’ lineup? Dave Roberts is ‘open’ to it
- Click here to listen to this article
ATLANTA — As the Dodgers mull potential lineup changes for Game 3 of the National League Division Series, manager Dave Roberts said he is “open” to moving Shohei Ohtani lower in the batting order.
In his three seasons with the Dodgers, Ohtani has batted first or second in every game he has started. However, as he has admitted he is trying to “manage” in the aftermath of knee and arm injuries, and as Roberts has acknowledged Ohtani is “not 100%,” the lack of success could compel the manager to replace him at the top of the lineup with a more productive hitter at some point.
“I would,” Roberts said Monday. “I would. I think it’s something that, you know, I think moving him from 1 to 2 — but going further than that? I’m open to it.
“And it’s something that if I do, I would obviously have the conversation with Shohei to explain why. And at the end of the day every conversation I’ve had with him is whatever’s best for the team, he’s all-in on. So I know that undoubtedly.”
It would be strange for the Dodgers to bench Shohei Ohtani, but it’s clear that pretending he’s healthy enough to provide meaningful at-bats isn’t helping.
The Dodgers are batting .215 through the first two games of the NLDS, with the Atlanta Braves scheduled to pitch left-handed ace Chris Sale in Game 3 on Tuesday. If the Dodgers lose, they would need to win back-to-back elimination games to advance beyond this series.
Roberts said the lineup changes he would consider include starting Kiké Hernández and Miguel Rojas, both of whom hit well against left-handers. That could mean infielders Max Muncy (0 for 7 against Sale, with five strikeouts) and Tommy Edman (0 for 11 against Sale) might not start.
Center fielder Andy Pages, who batted so poorly last October he was benched for the final three games of the World Series, is hitless in seven at-bats in this series, with four strikeouts.
“I’m gonna continue to give Andy leash,” Roberts said. “I believe in him. I feel that for us to win the World Series this year, we’re gonna need him to be an active part of our team.
Roberts said he did not envision benching catcher Will Smith, who is 0 for 8 in the series. The Dodgers’ backup catcher, Hunter Feduccia, is a career .205 hitter with no postseason experience.
But, even with the Dodgers’ star-studded lineup, the spotlight shines brightest on Ohtani.
Ohtani has not homered since Aug. 18. He hit .157 between then and the end of the regular season, striking out in 41% of his at-bats. In this series, he has two hits and two strikeouts in eight at-bats, and his inability to refrain from swinging at pitches outside the strike zone has become a glaring weakness.
“He’s not 100%,” Roberts said. “But, at the end of the day, he can still do a better job of staying in the strike zone.”
Ohtani hasn’t given the Braves a reason to challenge him within the strike zone.
“Everything orbits around Shohei, in the sense of his talent,” Roberts said. “And the Braves are going to enter with caution. And, so, knowing that, they’re going to continue to expand as long as we keep giving that to them. So until we show some discipline, they’re going to continue to kind of use that playbook.”
